docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Ninety seconds: install, bring your embeddings (any encoder, any modality), the dashboard from python app.py to the downloaded PDF, and the MCP call for agents.

ShortKit-ML measures the shortcut potential of a machine learning embedding with one calibrated audit and writes the result as an HTML or PDF report.

The audit answers one question: does the embedding carry a sensitive attribute (sex, age group, race, site, scanner) beyond what the task label explains? A conditional probe is the primary test, five secondary detectors are reported as diagnostics, and all six are calibrated by a permutation null that shuffles the attribute within task-label strata, so the probe decides at p < 0.05 and nothing else does.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Walkthrough

    The whole audit on one public data set, from a fresh install to the PDF report, in five terminal recordings and a dashboard video, all replayable on your own data.

    Walkthrough

  • Installation

    Clone and install from source with uv or pip. The audit module is newer than the PyPI release, so source is the way in for now.

    Installation

  • MCP server for agents

    Nine tools over stdio. run_audit runs the audit on files you name in chat, from Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any other MCP client.

    MCP server

  • The paper

    ShortKit-ML: an open toolkit for measuring shortcut potential in medical imaging embeddings. Preprint on medRxiv, with the method, the synthetic calibration and the clinical audits.

    Read the preprint

docs.title: What the audit needs
docs.text: Array Shape Meaning E (n, d) float one embedding per row, from any encoder, any width d A (n,) the sensitive attribute Y (n,) the task label the classifier would learn groups (n,), optional a unit id (patient, identity) when one unit has several rows

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from shortcut_detect.audit import AuditConfig, conditional_audit
from shortcut_detect.audit.report import audit_report

E = np.load("embeddings.npy")   # (n, d), any encoder
A = np.load("attribute.npy")    # (n,)
Y = np.load("labels.npy")       # (n,)
result = conditional_audit(E, A, Y, config=AuditConfig(seed=42))  # groups=patient_ids when needed
print(result.results["probe"].p_value)
audit_report(result, "audit.pdf", attribute="sex", task="pneumonia")

The dashboard, the 19 exploratory detectors and the mitigation methods are documented under Other package methods.

docs.title: Benchmark methods
docs.text: This document records the method selection of the earlier fixed-threshold benchmark (13 methods compared against fixed thresholds) and how to replay it. The paper scores six calibrated detectors instead, with the conditional probe as the single primary test; see Results below and the paper's pipeline.

docs.title: What the paper scores
docs.text: Of the 19 registered detection methods, six need only the embedding, the attribute and the task label and are calibrated by the conditional permutation null: the conditional probe (primary) and the statistical, geometric, bias direction PCA, HBAC and frequency detectors (secondary, same null, reported as diagnostics). The number of flagged detectors in a cell is descriptive only; no agreement threshold is used. SIS is outside the score (it fits on the task label with a fixed 15% subset and has no attribute-aware form). Demographic parity, equalized odds and intersectional gaps are computed only for the trained heads of the classification-head experiment, and GroupDRO, GCE, SSA, early-epoch clustering, CAV, SpRAy, GradCAM, causal effect, the CVAE and the VAE contribute to no result in the paper.

docs.title: Earlier benchmark method selection
docs.text: Of the 19 registered detection methods, 13 were benchmarked in the earlier fixed-threshold benchmark. The remaining 6 require raw images, concept sets, or specialized data loaders that are incompatible with the embedding-only evaluation protocol.

docs.title: Benchmarked methods (13, earlier benchmark)
docs.text: # Method Key Tier Paradigm What It Detects Detection Logic 1 HBAC hbac 1 Embedding Clustering by protected attributes report.has_shortcut.exists == True 2 Probe probe 1 Embedding Group info recoverable from embeddings results.shortcut_detected == True (F1 > threshold) 3 Statistical statistical 1 Embedding Dimensions with group differences Any significant features after FDR-BH correction 4 Geometric geometric 1 Representation Bias directions & prototype overlap summary.risk_level ∈ {moderate, high} 5 Frequency frequency 1 Embedding Signal concentrated in few dimensions report.shortcut_detected == True (TPR/FPR thresholds) 6 Bias Direction PCA bias_direction_pca 1 Representation Projection gap along bias direction report.risk_level ∈ {moderate, high} 7 SIS sis 1 Explainability Minimal dimensions sufficient for prediction shortcut_detected == True (frac_dims ≤ 0.15) 8 Demographic Parity demographic_parity 2 Fairness Prediction rate disparities across groups report.risk_level ∈ {moderate, high} 9 Equalized Odds equalized_odds 2 Fairness TPR/FPR disparities across groups report.risk_level ∈ {moderate, high} 10 Intersectional intersectional 2 Fairness Intersectional fairness gaps (2+ attributes) report.risk_level ∈ {moderate, high} 11 GroupDRO groupdro 3 Training Dynamics Worst-group performance gaps avg_acc - worst_group_acc > 0.10 12 GCE gce 3 Training Dynamics High-loss minority/bias-conflicting samples report.risk_level ∈ {moderate, high} 13 SSA ssa 3 Training Dynamics Spurious attribute spread shortcut_detected == True

docs.title: Tiers explained
docs.text:
Tier Name Requirements Methods 1 Embedding-native embeddings + labels + group_labels hbac, probe, statistical, geometric, frequency, bias_direction_pca, sis 2 Fairness-based embeddings + binary labels + protected_labels demographic_parity, equalized_odds, intersectional 3 Training-dynamics embeddings + labels + group_labels (trains internal model) groupdro, gce, ssa

All 13 methods work with the ShortcutDetector.fit(embeddings, labels, group_labels=g) API. No raw images, model weights, or external data required.

docs.title: Excluded methods (6) and why
docs.text: Method Key Why Excluded Could Be Included? CAV cav Requires concept activation sets via fit_from_loaders() Only with manually curated concept sets GradCAM Mask Overlap gradcam_mask_overlap Requires raw images + model with gradients Only with image data + model access Early Epoch Clustering early_epoch_clustering Requires epoch-by-epoch representations during training Only during model training VAE vae Trains a VAE; expensive and noisy on small samples Possible but slow (~minutes per run on 2K samples) Generative CVAE generative_cvae Trains a CVAE counterfactual generator Possible but very slow Causal Effect causal_effect Requires interventional data via fit_from_loaders() Only with causal/interventional data

docs.title: Special cases
docs.text:
• Intersectional: Requires extra_labels with 2+ demographic attributes. Skipped in synthetic benchmarks (1 attribute only) and in CheXpert per-diagnosis (single attribute tested). Works on MIMIC-CXR (sex + race + age_bin) and CelebA (40 attributes).
  • GroupDRO: Detection threshold is avg_acc - worst_group_acc > 0.10 (10% gap). In practice, GroupDRO reports success=False on most benchmark runs because its internal training doesn't converge or produce a meaningful gap with pre-extracted embeddings. It was designed for end-to-end training scenarios. Effectively 0 detections in benchmarks.
  • GCE: Reports risk=high on most runs but doesn't meet the flagging threshold via method_flag() because its risk_level in the report dict stays at "low". GCE is designed to identify high-loss minority samples; on pre-extracted embeddings with binary labels, the loss landscape is shallow. Effectively 0 detections in benchmarks.
  • SSA: Requires a splits parameter (labeled/unlabeled split indices) that the benchmark scripts don't provide. Fails with "splits parameter required for SSA analysis". Effectively 0 detections in benchmarks.
  • Net effect of Tier 3 methods: GroupDRO, GCE, and SSA are included for completeness (the Gradio demo runs them) but they add 0 detections in the embedding-only benchmark protocol. The effective detection count is X/13 where the 3 Tier 3 methods always report "not flagged." This is documented honestly: these methods were designed for training-time scenarios, not post-hoc embedding analysis.

docs.title: Replaying the earlier benchmark
docs.text: The commands below rerun the 13-method protocol. The old stage of scripts/revision/run_all.sh reruns its clinical tables with the fixed flag reader for the comparison in the paper.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/criticaldata/ShortKit-ML.git
cd ShortKit-ML
pip install -e ".[all]"

# Download embeddings (gated: request access on the dataset page with your PhysioNet
# username; proof of MIMIC-CXR access is required before approval)
huggingface-cli download MITCriticalData/ShortKit-ML-data --repo-type dataset --local-dir data/

docs.title: Run benchmarks (one at a time)
docs.text:
# 1. CheXpert: 7 backbones × 3 attributes × 13 methods + per-diagnosis
python scripts/run_chexpert_multibackbone_benchmark.py
# Output: output/paper_benchmark/chexpert_multibackbone_results/

# 2. MIMIC-CXR: 4 backbones × 3 attributes × 13 methods
python scripts/run_mimic_benchmark.py
# Output: output/paper_benchmark/mimic_cxr_results/

# 3. CelebA: 3 shortcut pairs × 13 methods
python scripts/run_celeba_real_benchmark.py
# Output: output/paper_benchmark/celeba_real_results/

# 4. Cross-dataset per-diagnosis: 5 diagnoses × 3 conditions × 13 methods
python scripts/run_per_diagnosis_cross_dataset.py
# Output: output/paper_benchmark/cross_dataset_diagnosis/

# 5. Synthetic: 12 methods × effect size grid (smoke profile ~5 min)
python -m shortcut_detect.benchmark.paper_runner --config examples/paper_benchmark_config_reproducible.json
# Output: output/paper_benchmark/synthetic_10methods/

docs.title: Reproducibility guarantees
docs.text:
• Seed: All runs use seed=42
  • Data: Pre-extracted embeddings on HuggingFace (no GPU needed)
  • Determinism: NumPy/scikit-learn random states fixed per method
  • CI: the test suite runs on Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 (GitHub Actions)

docs.title: Results
docs.text: The 13-method detection-rate summary from the earlier benchmark is superseded. The paper reports a conditional audit (the conditional probe as primary test, five secondary detectors sharing its permutation null, BH correction within a cell) instead; its tables and figures are built by the paper's pipeline and written to output/paper_tables/revision/, with the resolved numbers in numbers.json there.

docs.title: Method implementation conventions
docs.text:
To keep detection methods consistent across contributors, follow these project conventions:

  • File naming: Prefer {method}_detector.py for modules whose primary purpose is a single detector class.
  • Config classes: For detectors with multiple constructor parameters, use a frozen dataclass config (for example MyMethodConfig) and expose it as an optional config= argument.
  • Probe reuse: Reuse shared probe implementations (SKLearnProbe / TorchProbe) instead of re-implementing standalone probe training logic inside method modules.
  • Shared validation/helpers: Reuse common utilities (for example validate_embeddings_labels) instead of duplicating shape/length validation helpers across files.

If a method needs a deviation from these rules, document the reason in the module docstring and PR description.

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
# Run all tests
pytest tests/ -v

# Run with coverage (requires pytest-cov)
pytest tests/ --cov=shortcut_detect --cov-report=html

Note: Coverage requires pytest-cov which is included when you install with pip install -e ".[all]" or pip install -e ".[dev]".

# Run specific test file
pytest tests/test_probes.py -v

# Run specific test
pytest tests/test_probes.py::TestSKLearnProbe::test_sklearn_probe_basic_shortcut_detected -v

docs.title: Writing tests
docs.text:
Tests are in the tests/ directory. Use pytest fixtures for common setup:

# tests/test_my_feature.py
import pytest
import numpy as np
from shortcut_detect import ShortcutDetector

@pytest.fixture
def sample_data():
    """Generate sample data for testing."""
    np.random.seed(42)
    X = np.random.randn(100, 50)
    y = np.random.randint(0, 2, 100)
    return X, y

def test_detector_fit(sample_data):
    """Test that detector fits without error."""
    X, y = sample_data
    detector = ShortcutDetector(methods=['probe'])
    detector.fit(X, y)
    assert 'probe' in detector.results_

docs.title: Building docs locally
docs.text:
You can build docs in a separate virtual environment to avoid conflicts with your main development environment:

# Create a separate docs environment (recommended)
python -m venv .venv-docs
source .venv-docs/bin/activate  # Windows: .venv-docs\Scripts\activate

# Install only docs dependencies (no need for the full package)
pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]" pymdown-extensions

# Serve docs locally
mkdocs serve
# Visit http://127.0.0.1:8000

# Build static site
mkdocs build

# Deploy to GitHub Pages
mkdocs gh-deploy

Alternatively, install docs dependencies in your main environment:

pip install -e ".[docs]"
mkdocs serve

docs.title: Writing documentation
docs.text:
• Documentation is in docs/ using Markdown
  • API docs auto-generated from docstrings via mkdocstrings
  • Follow Google docstring style

Example docstring:

def fit(self, embeddings: np.ndarray, group_labels: np.ndarray) -> "ShortcutDetector":
    """Fit the shortcut detector on embeddings.

    Args:
        embeddings: Array of shape (n_samples, n_features) containing
            the embedding vectors to analyze.
        group_labels: Array of shape (n_samples,) containing the
            protected attribute labels for each sample.

    Returns:
        Self, for method chaining.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If embeddings and group_labels have mismatched lengths.

    Example:
        >>> detector = ShortcutDetector()
        >>> detector.fit(embeddings, group_labels)
        >>> print(detector.summary())
    """

docs.title: Adding a method to the leaderboard
docs.text: The quickest way to contribute a detection or mitigation method, from any modality the benchmark covers, is a leaderboard submission: one folder under contrib/ with a method.py, no changes to the package. See Submit a method. The section below is for methods that should also become part of the ShortcutDetector API.

docs.title: Adding new detection methods
docs.text: Start from the template. Copy shortcut_detect/detector_template.py into your method's package and rename the classes. The template contains inline comments for every required step and produces valid Python that you can run immediately.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A detection method in this library consists of two pieces:

Piece Base class Purpose Standalone detector DetectorBase Runs the algorithm, stores results in the standardized results_ dict Builder / runner BaseDetector Constructs the detector and integrates it with the ShortcutDetector orchestrator

Both are demonstrated in the template file.

docs.title: Required results_ schema
docs.text:
Every detector must populate results_ via _set_results(). The schema is:

{
    "method": str,                # unique snake_case identifier
    "shortcut_detected": bool | None,  # True / False / None
    "risk_level": "low" | "moderate" | "high" | "unknown",
    "metrics": {                  # small scalar values only
        "score": 0.42,
    },
    "notes": str,                 # human-readable explanation
    "metadata": {                 # config, dataset info
        "threshold": 0.5,
        "n_samples": 1000,
    },
    # optional:
    "report": { ... },            # detailed structured output
    "details": { ... },           # large / auxiliary data
}

Guidelines:

  • metrics: keep small and scalar (floats, ints, short strings). Arrays, tables, and large objects belong in report or details.
  • risk_level: use "unknown" if the method cannot assess risk. The legacy value "medium" is automatically mapped to "moderate".
  • shortcut_detected: use None if detection logic is not yet implemented.

docs.title: 1. Copy the template
docs.text:
# Create your method package
mkdir -p shortcut_detect/my_method
cp shortcut_detect/detector_template.py shortcut_detect/my_method/detector.py

docs.title: 2. Implement the standalone detector
docs.text:
In shortcut_detect/my_method/detector.py, rename MyMethodDetector and fill in the fit() method. The key contract inside fit() is:

def fit(self, embeddings, labels, group_labels):
    # 1. Validate inputs
    # 2. Run your detection algorithm
    # 3. Determine shortcut_detected (bool | None)
    # 4. Assess risk_level (RiskLevel enum or string)
    # 5. Call self._set_results(...)
    # 6. Set self._is_fitted = True
    # 7. Return self

docs.title: 3. Implement the builder (optional but recommended)
docs.text:
The builder lets the ShortcutDetector orchestrator run your method alongside others. Implement build() (returns an unfitted detector) and run() (fits it and returns a summary dict).

The dict returned by run() must have this shape:

{
    "detector": detector,          # the fitted DetectorBase instance
    "results": detector.results_,  # the standardized results_ dict
    "summary_title": "My Method",  # short title for reports
    "summary_lines": [...],        # list of human-readable lines
    "risk_indicators": [...],      # list of risk strings (can be empty)
    "success": True,               # False if the method failed
}

docs.title: 4. Register with the package
docs.text:
# shortcut_detect/my_method/__init__.py
from .detector import MyMethodDetector

__all__ = ["MyMethodDetector"]

# shortcut_detect/__init__.py  (add to existing exports)
from .my_method import MyMethodDetector

docs.title: 5. Integrate with ShortcutDetector
docs.text:
Builders are registered through a plugin module that ShortcutDetector imports lazily by method name. Add a plugin.py next to your detector and list it in _METHOD_PLUGIN_MODULES in shortcut_detect/discovery.py:

# shortcut_detect/my_method/plugin.py
from ..unified import DetectorFactory
from .builder import MyMethodBuilder

DetectorFactory.register("my_method", MyMethodBuilder)

# shortcut_detect/discovery.py  (add to _METHOD_PLUGIN_MODULES)
"my_method": "shortcut_detect.my_method.plugin",

docs.title: 6. Add tests
docs.text:
# tests/test_my_method.py
import numpy as np
from shortcut_detect.my_method import MyMethodDetector

def test_my_method_basic():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
    X = rng.standard_normal((100, 50))
    y = rng.integers(0, 2, 100)
    g = rng.integers(0, 3, 100)

    detector = MyMethodDetector(threshold=0.5)
    detector.fit(X, y, g)

    assert detector._is_fitted
    assert detector.results_["method"] == "my_method"
    assert "metrics" in detector.results_
    assert detector.results_["risk_level"] in ("low", "moderate", "high", "unknown")
    assert isinstance(detector.shortcut_detected_, (bool, type(None)))

docs.title: MCP Server
docs.text:
ShortKit-ML ships a Model Context Protocol server, shortcut_detect.mcp_server, that speaks MCP over stdio. An assistant connected to it (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, GitHub Copilot in VS Code, or any other MCP client) can run the audit on files you name in chat, with no Python script.

The server registers nine tools. run_audit is the audit of the paper, shortcut_detect.audit.conditional_audit: one conditional probe calibrated by a permutation null, which decides at p < 0.05, plus five secondary detectors that are descriptive. The other eight tools wrap the older ShortcutDetector pipeline (19 methods, fixed thresholds, risk-level verdicts). The paper withdrew those verdicts; the tools stay for exploration and are described in the last section.

docs.title: Install and check
docs.text:
uv pip install -e ".[mcp]"
.venv/bin/python -m shortcut_detect.mcp_server

The second command starts the server and waits for a client on stdin, so it prints nothing. Press Ctrl+C to stop it. shortkit-ml-mcp is the same entry point installed as a console script.

docs.title: The run_audit tool
docs.text:
run_audit reads the four arrays of the audit from files and returns one JSON object. It never takes inline arrays: embeddings are too large for a chat message, and a file path is what an agent can pass without copying data through the model.

Argument Required Meaning embeddings_path yes E, an (n, d) matrix. .npy, .npz with one array, .csv, .tsv or .txt attribute_path yes A, one value per row, strings or integers (sex, 0/1, site) task_path yes Y, one value per row, strings or integers; the audit conditions on it groups_path no patient ids, one per row; makes folds, bootstrap and permutations patient-level n_permutations no K for the five secondary detectors, default 200 n_permutations_probe no K for the probe; defaults to n_permutations. The paper's clinical audits used 500 seed no default 0 attribute, task no names used in the summary and the report, for example sex and pneumothorax report_path no .html or .pdf; written with shortcut_detect.audit.report.audit_report

A CSV label file may carry a header row. A file of string labels must have one, because its first row is read as the header. The task label is encoded to integer codes in sorted order of its levels; task_levels in the output gives that order. Both A and Y need at least two levels.

docs.title: Worked call
docs.text:
In chat, you write something like this:

Run the ShortKit-ML audit on /data/cxr/E.npy with attribute /data/cxr/sex.csv and
task /data/cxr/pneumothorax.csv. Call them sex and pneumothorax, use 500 probe
permutations and 200 for the rest, and write the report to /data/cxr/audit.pdf.

The assistant then calls the tool with these arguments:

{
  "embeddings_path": "/data/cxr/E.npy",
  "attribute_path": "/data/cxr/sex.csv",
  "task_path": "/data/cxr/pneumothorax.csv",
  "attribute": "sex",
  "task": "pneumothorax",
  "n_permutations": 200,
  "n_permutations_probe": 500,
  "seed": 0,
  "report_path": "/data/cxr/audit.pdf"
}

The same call from Python, which is what the test suite exercises:

from shortcut_detect.mcp_server import run_audit

print(run_audit(
    embeddings_path="/data/cxr/E.npy",
    attribute_path="/data/cxr/sex.csv",
    task_path="/data/cxr/pneumothorax.csv",
    attribute="sex", task="pneumothorax",
    n_permutations=200, n_permutations_probe=500,
    report_path="/data/cxr/audit.pdf",
))

Abridged output (synthetic data, 300 rows, 16 dimensions, K = 20, where the attribute was planted in one dimension):

{
  "attribute": "sex",
  "task": "pneumothorax",
  "n": 300,
  "n_groups": 2,
  "attribute_levels": ["female", "male"],
  "task_levels": ["0", "1"],
  "group_sizes": {"Y=0,A=female": 64, "Y=0,A=male": 82, "Y=1,A=female": 84, "Y=1,A=male": 70},
  "probe": {
    "statistic": 0.817,
    "ci_low": 0.768,
    "ci_high": 0.858,
    "null_mean": 0.514,
    "null_sd": 0.049,
    "p_value": 0.048,
    "flag": true,
    "n_permutations": 20
  },
  "detectors": [
    {"detector": "probe", "statistic": 0.817, "p_value": 0.048, "flag": true, "...": "..."},
    {"detector": "statistical", "...": "..."},
    {"detector": "geometric", "...": "..."},
    {"detector": "bias_direction", "...": "..."},
    {"detector": "hbac_nmi", "...": "..."},
    {"detector": "frequency_topk", "...": "..."}
  ],
  "n_flagged": 6,
  "summary": "The conditional probe predicts sex from the embedding and pneumothorax; its out-of-fold AUROC is 0.817 (95% CI 0.768 to 0.858) against a permutation null of 0.514 (SD 0.049, 20 permutations of sex within levels of pneumothorax), p = 0.048. At alpha = 0.05 the embedding carries information about sex beyond what pneumothorax explains ...",
  "report_path": "/data/cxr/audit.pdf"
}

probe is the decision: out-of-fold AUROC of the conditional probe, its bootstrap 95% interval, the mean and SD of the permutation null, the permutation p-value and the flag (p below 0.05). detectors holds the six rows of AuditResult.rows(), one per detector, with the same statistics plus the Benjamini-Hochberg q (p_bh) for the five secondaries, the run time in seconds, and the fold strata and attribute level used. n_flagged counts flagged rows across all six and is descriptive. summary is the paragraph of summary_text, the same text that heads the report. Quantities that do not exist for a detector (the statistical detector has no CI, the probe has no q) come back as null.

Twenty permutations on 300 rows of 16 dimensions take a few seconds on a laptop; the cost grows about linearly with K and with n.

docs.title: Register the server
docs.text: Every client runs the same command, .venv/bin/python -m shortcut_detect.mcp_server, from the repo root. Use the interpreter inside .venv: a bare python or uv run resolves to a different interpreter in Claude Desktop, where shortcut_detect is not installed.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
The repo ships .mcp.json, so a Claude Code session opened from the repo root already sees the server. On first use Claude Code asks you to approve the project server; until then claude mcp list shows it as Pending approval (run claude to approve).

To register it yourself, or in another checkout:

claude mcp add --scope project shortkit-ml .venv/bin/python -- -m shortcut_detect.mcp_server

This writes .mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "shortkit-ml": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": ".venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "shortcut_detect.mcp_server"],
      "env": {}
    }
  }
}

Check with claude mcp list. Once approved the line reads:

shortkit-ml: .venv/bin/python -m shortcut_detect.mcp_server - ✓ Connected

docs.title: Claude Desktop (macOS)
docs.text:
Claude Desktop does not inherit your shell PATH, so the command needs the absolute path of the interpreter. Find it with echo $(pwd)/.venv/bin/python from the repo root, then add the block to ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "shortkit-ml": {
      "command": "/Users/yourname/ShortKit-ML/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "shortcut_detect.mcp_server"],
      "cwd": "/Users/yourname/ShortKit-ML"
    }
  }
}

Replace /Users/yourname/ShortKit-ML with your checkout. Restart Claude Desktop; the shortkit-ml tools then appear in the tools panel.

Error Cause Fix Server disconnected bare uv or python used as command use the full .venv/bin/python path ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp' mcp not installed in .venv uv pip install -e ".[mcp]" ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'shortcut_detect' uv run used as command; it picks its own managed Python use .venv/bin/python directly

docs.title: GitHub Copilot in VS Code
docs.text:
The repo ships .vscode/mcp.json, read by Copilot Chat in Agent mode when the repo root is the open workspace:

{
  "servers": {
    "shortkit-ml": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": ".venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "shortcut_detect.mcp_server"]
    }
  }
}

Open Copilot Chat, switch the mode dropdown to Agent, and open the tools list; the shortkit-ml server and its tools should be there. If VS Code cannot find the interpreter, replace command with the absolute path of your .venv/bin/python. The config and its test (tests/test_copilot_mcp_config.py) are in place; the Copilot Chat smoke test itself still needs a confirmation in VS Code by running a real prompt.

docs.title: Agent environments
docs.text: The paper's conclusion names DOJO (Distributed Open Justice Oversight, Xiang et al. 2026), a community-driven platform for adversarial evaluation of health AI, as a setting where the audit would run as one of the embedding-level checks. The MCP server is the hook for that kind of environment: an agent holding an embedding matrix, an attribute, a task label and optional patient ids calls run_audit over MCP with the same four arrays, as files, and gets back the calibrated result, the summary and the report that the Python API gives.

docs.title: Exploratory tools (the legacy pipeline)
docs.text:
The remaining eight tools run the first-submission ShortcutDetector pipeline: 19 methods, each with a fixed threshold and a low, moderate or high risk level, combined by majority vote. The paper withdrew those verdicts in favour of the calibrated audit above, so treat these tools as a way to look at individual method statistics, not as a decision. Each tool's description in the server says so.

Tool What it does list_methods the 19 methods with one-line descriptions generate_synthetic_data a synthetic dataset (linear, nonlinear or none, configurable strength) as inline arrays run_detector runs chosen methods on embeddings; returns a verdict, a risk level and a per-method breakdown get_summary the text summary of a previous run_detector session get_method_detail the raw result dict of one method from a session compare_methods side-by-side table and majority vote across methods generate_report HTML, PDF or Markdown report of a session, optionally base64-encoded run_benchmark the synthetic benchmark grid through BenchmarkRunner

run_detector and compare_methods take embeddings, labels and group labels inline or as file paths (embeddings_path, labels_path, group_labels_path; same formats as run_audit). Labels are cast to integers. Default methods are hbac, probe and statistical for run_detector and those plus geometric and demographic_parity for compare_methods.

Prompts that reach these tools:

List the ShortKit-ML detection methods.
Generate 200 synthetic samples with a linear shortcut (strength 0.8) and run probe, statistical and hbac on them.
Run the detector on my embeddings at ~/data/embeddings.npy with labels at ~/data/labels.npy and group labels at ~/data/group_labels.npy.
Compare all default methods on 300 nonlinear shortcut samples. Which ones agree?
Show me the raw results for hbac from the last run.
Generate an HTML report for the last detector run and give me the file path.
Run the ShortKit-ML synthetic benchmark and show me the results.

Sessions of run_detector are cached under ~/.cache/shortkit-ml-mcp/ with joblib and survive a server restart; pass session_id to name one and get_summary, get_method_detail and generate_report read it back. Each MCP client gets its own sessions. run_audit keeps no session: its result is the JSON it returns and the report it writes.

Claude Desktop running the 19 legacy methods on a synthetic dataset through run_detector. The HIGH RISK verdict shown is the legacy pipeline's majority vote, not the audit's decision.

docs.title: Reproducing the paper's results
docs.text: This guide explains how to reproduce the results of the ShortKit-ML paper. The paper's pipeline is in The paper's pipeline below. The smoke, default and full profiles in the next sections run the earlier synthetic benchmark (fixed-threshold detectors) and do not produce the paper's tables.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10, 3.11, or 3.12
  • pip or uv package manager
  • (Optional) Docker for fully isolated runs

docs.title: 1. Install the package
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/criticaldata/ShortKit-ML.git
cd ShortKit-ML
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: 2. Run the reproducibility script
docs.text:
# Quick sanity check
./scripts/reproduce_paper.sh smoke

# Moderate run (recommended first attempt)
./scripts/reproduce_paper.sh default

# Full synthetic grid
./scripts/reproduce_paper.sh full

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Profile Grid size Seeds Expected runtime smoke 2 effect sizes, 1 sample size, 1 dim 2 2-5 minutes default 4 effect sizes, 2 sample sizes, 2 dims 3+ 15-30 minutes full 5 effect sizes, 3 sample sizes, 3 dims 10 2-4 hours

All profiles use random_seed: 42 for deterministic results.

docs.title: Using Docker
docs.text:
For a fully isolated, reproducible environment:

# Build the image
docker build -t shortcut-detect .

# Run with a specific profile (output is mounted to the host)
docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/output:/app/output shortcut-detect smoke
docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/output:/app/output shortcut-detect default
docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/output:/app/output shortcut-detect full

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The reproducible config is at examples/paper_benchmark_config_reproducible.json. It explicitly specifies every parameter so there is no ambiguity:

  • random_seed: 42 (fixed for all runs)
  • methods: hbac, probe, statistical, geometric
  • effect_sizes: 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.2, 2.0 (Cohen's d)
  • sample_sizes: 200, 1000, 5000
  • imbalance_ratios: 0.5 (balanced), 0.9 (imbalanced)
  • embedding_dims: 128, 256, 512
  • shortcut_dims: 5
  • seeds: 10 independent seeds per configuration
  • alpha: 0.05
  • corrections: bonferroni, fdr_bh

For custom runs, copy the config and modify as needed, then call:

python -m shortcut_detect.benchmark.paper_runner --config your_config.json

docs.title: Expected output files
docs.text:
After a successful run, the timestamped output directory contains:

File Description synthetic_runs.csv Raw results for every synthetic configuration synthetic_power_recall.csv Power/recall analysis across effect sizes synthetic_false_positive.csv False positive rates under the null correction_comparison.csv Multiple testing correction comparison benchmark_meta.json Run metadata (config, timing, environment)

docs.title: CheXpert (dataset 2)
docs.text: The CheXpert real-data benchmark requires access to the CheXpert dataset. Set chexpert.enabled: true and provide chexpert.manifest_path in the config. See scripts/extract_chexpert_embeddings.py for embedding extraction.

docs.title: The paper's pipeline
docs.text:
Every table, figure and number of the paper comes from one pipeline:

./scripts/reproduce_paper.sh revision          # all stages
scripts/revision/run_all.sh head mlp tables    # selected stages

Stages, in order: old clinical negctl synthetic nullcheck head dfr mlp race analyses umap marker extraction alignment overlap sensitivity sample_vs_full nlprobe nlprobe_clinical scaling tables. The race stage repeats the head experiment with race (White against non-White) as the attribute, logistic head only. The sensitivity stage runs the probe checks C, frontal and labelled. The sample_vs_full stage compares the audited CheXpert sample with the full train.csv on sex, age, view and race. The nlprobe stage runs the conditional probe on squared and pairwise-product features of the synthetic embeddings, under the same permutation null, at one small setting (nonlinear_probe/). The nlprobe_clinical stage fits the probe on [E, E^2] for every primary cell of the clinical audit (CheXpert and MIMIC-CXR, not CelebA) with the audit's seed, K = 500, patient-grouped folds and permutation draws, and joins the linear probe's AUROC and decision from clinical_audit/ (nonlinear_probe_clinical/); the pairwise-product design is not run at d up to 2048. The scaling stage times the probe alone (K = 500, patient-grouped folds) on synthetic 768-dimensional embeddings at 2,000 to 50,000 images and fits a log-log slope (probe_scaling/). One more stage runs only when named: prepare_mimic rebuilds data/mimic_cxr/vit32_cls_embeddings_realigned.npy and mimic_race_raw.csv from the coreset parquet files in mimic_cxr/source/ of the ShortKit-ML-data dataset (downloaded from the hub, or a local copy through QML_DIR; needs pyarrow). The Stored array column of the sensitivity table reads clinical_audit_stored_arrays/, which no stage writes: it is a frozen output of the clinical stage from before the CheXpert switch to the public/ arrays. Results go to ~/Documents/shortkit-ml-results/2026-10-28_revision_<commit>/ unless SHORTKIT_REVISION_DIR is set; each stage writes a MANIFEST.txt with the commit, data hashes and settings. tables writes the LaTeX tables, figures and numbers.tex to output/paper_tables/revision/.

The embeddings come from the gated dataset MITCriticalData/ShortKit-ML-data. To get access, click Request access on the dataset page and include your PhysioNet username; proof of current MIMIC-CXR access is required (never share your password). Requests are approved by hand.

The audit in every stage is shortcut_detect.audit.conditional_audit: the conditional probe (L2 logistic regression predicting the attribute from the embedding and the task label, out-of-fold AUROC) is the single primary test, calibrated by permuting the attribute within task-label strata and between patients (K=500 in the clinical audits, 200 for the secondary detectors, the synthetic grid and the audits after mitigation). The five secondary detectors share that null; the six p-values of a cell are Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted, and the count of flagged detectors is descriptive only. The audit reports shortcut potential; the classification-head experiment (head, mlp, race, dfr stages) tests separately whether a head trained on confounded data uses the attribute.

For CheXpert the pipeline reads ResNet-50, DenseNet-121 and ViT-B/16 from data/chexpert_multibackbone/, and ViT-B/32, DINOv2, RAD-DINO and MedSigLIP-448 from data/chexpert_multibackbone/public/. The extraction stage regenerates the public/ arrays from the CheXpert images with pinned public checkpoints (it needs torch 2.6 or later with transformers, set through EXTRACT_PYTHON, and accepted terms for google/medsiglip-448). The CheXpert sample is the first 2,000 images in the order of the official train.csv (477 patients, 423 lateral views); sex comes from train.csv, race per patient from the demographics file (White against non-White in the primary analysis, 217 images without a usable race record left out), and the task is Pneumothorax. MIMIC-CXR has 1,491 subjects with one image each, task in-hospital mortality, with four backbones: RAD-DINO, ViT-B/16, ViT-B/32 (rebuilt from the source in metadata order) and MedSigLIP-448. The source README names google/siglip-so400m-patch14-384 for that array, but re-embedding 50 of its images with google/medsiglip-448 reproduces the stored vectors (cosine 1.000), so it is reported as MedSigLIP.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Import errors: Make sure the package is installed with pip install -e ".[dev]".
  • PyTorch/CUDA: For GPU support, install PyTorch separately following pytorch.org.
  • PDF export errors: Install system libraries for weasyprint: brew install pango gdk-pixbuf libffi (macOS) or apt-get install libpango1.0-dev libgdk-pixbuf2.0-dev libffi-dev (Debian/Ubuntu).

docs.title: AdversarialDebiasing
docs.text:
AdversarialDebiasing(
    hidden_dim: int | None = None,
    adversary_weight: float = 0.5,
    n_epochs: int = 50,
    batch_size: int = 64,
    lr: float = 0.001,
    dropout: float = 0.1,
    device: str | device | None = None,
    random_state: int | None = None,
)

Adversarial debiasing to remove demographic encoding from embeddings (Zhang et al. 2018).

Trains an encoder that maps embeddings to a hidden representation, with an adversary (via Gradient Reversal Layer) trying to predict the protected attribute from that representation. The encoder learns to be informative for the task while uninformative for the protected attribute.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
hidden_dim : int, optional Hidden dimension of the encoder. If None, uses min(64, embed_dim). adversary_weight : float Weight (lambda) for the adversarial loss. Higher values push harder to remove protected-attribute information. Default 0.5. n_epochs : int Number of training epochs. batch_size : int Batch size for training. lr : float Learning rate. dropout : float Dropout rate in the encoder. device : str or torch.device, optional Device to train on. Defaults to cuda if available else cpu. random_state : int, optional Seed for reproducibility.

Source code in shortcut_detect/mitigation/adversarial_debiasing.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    hidden_dim: int | None = None,
    adversary_weight: float = 0.5,
    n_epochs: int = 50,
    batch_size: int = 64,
    lr: float = 1e-3,
    dropout: float = 0.1,
    device: str | torch.device | None = None,
    random_state: int | None = None,
):
    self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
    self.adversary_weight = float(adversary_weight)
    self.n_epochs = int(n_epochs)
    self.batch_size = int(batch_size)
    self.lr = float(lr)
    self.dropout = float(dropout)
    self.device = device
    self.random_state = random_state

    self._encoder: nn.Module | None = None
    self._adversary: nn.Module | None = None
    self._task_head: nn.Module | None = None
    self._embed_dim: int | None = None
    self._n_protected: int | None = None
    self._n_task: int | None = None
    self._fitted = False

docs.title: fit
docs.text:
fit(
    embeddings: ndarray,
    protected_labels: ndarray,
    task_labels: ndarray | None = None,
) -> AdversarialDebiasing

Fit the adversarial debiasing model.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: embeddings : np.ndarray Shape (n_samples, embed_dim). protected_labels : np.ndarray Shape (n_samples,) – demographic/protected attribute labels. task_labels : np.ndarray, optional Shape (n_samples,) – task labels. If provided, the encoder also minimizes task loss to preserve utility.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
self : AdversarialDebiasing

Source code in shortcut_detect/mitigation/adversarial_debiasing.py 
def fit(
    self,
    embeddings: np.ndarray,
    protected_labels: np.ndarray,
    task_labels: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> AdversarialDebiasing:
    """
    Fit the adversarial debiasing model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    embeddings : np.ndarray
        Shape (n_samples, embed_dim).
    protected_labels : np.ndarray
        Shape (n_samples,) – demographic/protected attribute labels.
    task_labels : np.ndarray, optional
        Shape (n_samples,) – task labels. If provided, the encoder also
        minimizes task loss to preserve utility.

    Returns
    -------
    self : AdversarialDebiasing
    """
    self._setup_seed()
    X = np.asarray(embeddings, dtype=np.float32)
    s = np.asarray(protected_labels)
    if X.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError("embeddings must be 2D (n_samples, embed_dim)")
    if s.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError("protected_labels must be 1D")
    if X.shape[0] != s.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("embeddings and protected_labels must have same length")

    embed_dim = X.shape[1]
    uniq = np.unique(s)
    n_protected = len(uniq)
    s_map = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(uniq)}
    s_idx = np.array([s_map[v] for v in s], dtype=np.int64)

    n_task: int | None = None
    y_idx: np.ndarray | None = None
    if task_labels is not None:
        y = np.asarray(task_labels)
        if y.ndim != 1 or y.shape[0] != X.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError("task_labels must be 1D with same length as embeddings")
        y_uniq = np.unique(y)
        n_task = len(y_uniq)
        y_map = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(y_uniq)}
        y_idx = np.array([y_map[v] for v in y], dtype=np.int64)

    h_dim = self.hidden_dim
    if h_dim is None:
        h_dim = min(64, embed_dim)

    device = self._device()
    encoder = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(embed_dim, h_dim),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Dropout(self.dropout),
    ).to(device)
    adversary = nn.Linear(h_dim, n_protected).to(device)
    task_head = nn.Linear(h_dim, n_task).to(device) if n_task is not None else None

    opt = torch.optim.Adam(
        list(encoder.parameters())
        + list(adversary.parameters())
        + (list(task_head.parameters()) if task_head is not None else []),
        lr=self.lr,
    )
    ce = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

    X_t = torch.from_numpy(X).float().to(device)
    s_t = torch.from_numpy(s_idx).long().to(device)
    if y_idx is not None:
        y_t = torch.from_numpy(y_idx).long().to(device)

    ds = TensorDataset(
        X_t,
        s_t,
        *((y_t,) if y_idx is not None else ()),
    )
    loader = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=self.batch_size, shuffle=True, drop_last=False)

    for _ in range(self.n_epochs):
        encoder.train()
        adversary.train()
        if task_head is not None:
            task_head.train()
        for batch in loader:
            x_b = batch[0]
            s_b = batch[1]
            y_b = batch[2] if len(batch) > 2 else None

            hidden = encoder(x_b)
            adv_in = _grl(hidden, self.adversary_weight)
            adv_logits = adversary(adv_in)
            loss_adv = ce(adv_logits, s_b)

            if task_head is not None and y_b is not None:
                task_logits = task_head(hidden)
                loss_task = ce(task_logits, y_b)
                loss = loss_task + loss_adv
            else:
                loss = loss_adv

            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss.backward()
            opt.step()

    self._encoder = encoder
    self._adversary = adversary
    self._task_head = task_head
    self._embed_dim = embed_dim
    self._n_protected = n_protected
    self._n_task = n_task
    self._fitted = True
    return self

docs.title: transform
docs.text:
transform(embeddings: ndarray) -> np.ndarray

Transform embeddings to debiased representations.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: embeddings : np.ndarray Shape (n_samples, embed_dim). Must match embed_dim from fit.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
np.ndarray Debiased embeddings, shape (n_samples, hidden_dim).

Source code in shortcut_detect/mitigation/adversarial_debiasing.py 
def transform(self, embeddings: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Transform embeddings to debiased representations.

    Parameters
    ----------
    embeddings : np.ndarray
        Shape (n_samples, embed_dim). Must match embed_dim from fit.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Debiased embeddings, shape (n_samples, hidden_dim).
    """
    if not self._fitted or self._encoder is None:
        raise ValueError("AdversarialDebiasing has not been fitted")
    X = np.asarray(embeddings, dtype=np.float32)
    if X.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError("embeddings must be 2D")
    if X.shape[1] != self._embed_dim:
        raise ValueError(
            f"embed_dim {X.shape[1]} does not match fitted embed_dim {self._embed_dim}"
        )

    device = self._device()
    self._encoder.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        x_t = torch.from_numpy(X).float().to(device)
        hidden = self._encoder(x_t)
        out = hidden.cpu().numpy()
    return out.astype(np.float64)

docs.title: fit_transform
docs.text:
fit_transform(
    embeddings: ndarray,
    protected_labels: ndarray,
    task_labels: ndarray | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray

Fit and transform in one step.

Source code in shortcut_detect/mitigation/adversarial_debiasing.py 
def fit_transform(
    self,
    embeddings: np.ndarray,
    protected_labels: np.ndarray,
    task_labels: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Fit and transform in one step."""
    self.fit(embeddings, protected_labels, task_labels=task_labels)
    return self.transform(embeddings)

docs.title: Audit API
docs.text: The audit module implements the attribute-aware shortcut-potential audit used in the paper: a conditional probe as the single primary test, five secondary detectors, and a conditional permutation null (the attribute shuffled within task-label strata, between patients when patient ids are given). See The paper's audit for the method description.

docs.title: Running an audit
docs.text:
from shortcut_detect.audit import AuditConfig, conditional_audit

cfg = AuditConfig(n_permutations=200, n_permutations_probe=500, seed=42)
result = conditional_audit(E, A, Y, config=cfg, groups=patient_ids)
probe = result.results["probe"]
print(probe.statistic, probe.p_value, probe.p_bh, probe.flag)

Settings fixed by the revision method decisions (sections 2 to 4).

docs.title: conditional_audit
docs.text:
conditional_audit(
    E: ndarray,
    A: ndarray,
    Y: ndarray,
    config: AuditConfig | None = None,
    groups: ndarray | None = None,
) -> AuditResult

Run the attribute-aware audit on one (embedding, attribute, task) cell.

E is any 2-D float matrix (n, d): any width d and any modality (image, text, audio, tabular, multimodal encoders), the audit only sees the numbers. A and Y are 1-D arrays of length n.

groups (e.g. patient ids) makes every cross-validation split patient-disjoint, every bootstrap resample whole patients, and the permutation patient-level within Y-pattern strata (see conditional_permutations).

Source code in shortcut_detect/audit/conditional.py 
def conditional_audit(
    E: np.ndarray,
    A: np.ndarray,
    Y: np.ndarray,
    config: AuditConfig | None = None,
    groups: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> AuditResult:
    """Run the attribute-aware audit on one (embedding, attribute, task) cell.

    ``E`` is any 2-D float matrix ``(n, d)``: any width ``d`` and any modality
    (image, text, audio, tabular, multimodal encoders), the audit only sees the
    numbers. ``A`` and ``Y`` are 1-D arrays of length ``n``.

    ``groups`` (e.g. patient ids) makes every cross-validation split
    patient-disjoint, every bootstrap resample whole patients, and the
    permutation patient-level within Y-pattern strata (see
    ``conditional_permutations``).
    """
    cfg = config or AuditConfig()
    # independent streams, so the observed statistic does not depend on K
    perm_ss, null_fold_ss, boot_ss, km_ss, cv_ss = np.random.SeedSequence(cfg.seed).spawn(5)
    perm_rng, null_fold_rng = np.random.default_rng(perm_ss), np.random.default_rng(null_fold_ss)
    boot_rng, km_rng = np.random.default_rng(boot_ss), np.random.default_rng(km_ss)
    cv_rng = np.random.default_rng(cv_ss if cfg.cv_seed is None else cfg.cv_seed)
    E = np.asarray(E)
    Y = np.asarray(Y).astype(np.int64)
    a, names = _encode(A)
    G = len(names)
    if G < 2:
        raise ValueError("the attribute needs at least two groups")
    if E.shape[0] != len(a) or len(a) != len(Y):
        raise ValueError("E, A and Y must have the same number of rows")
    groups_idx = None
    n_mixed = 0
    level = "image"
    if groups is not None:
        groups = np.asarray(groups)
        if len(groups) != len(a):
            raise ValueError("groups must have one entry per row")
        level = cfg.attribute_level
        if level == "patient":
            a, n_mixed = patient_majority(a, groups)
            if len(np.unique(a)) < 2:
                raise ValueError("the patient-level attribute needs at least two groups")
        _, ginv = np.unique(groups.astype(str), return_inverse=True)
        groups_idx = [np.flatnonzero(ginv == g) for g in range(ginv.max() + 1)]

    needs = set(cfg.detectors)
    ctx = _prepare(E, Y, cfg, needs, km_rng)
    ctx["G"] = G
    K = cfg.n_permutations
    Kp = cfg.n_permutations_probe or K
    k_max = max(K, Kp) if "probe" in needs else K
    a_rows = conditional_permutations(a, Y, k_max, perm_rng, cfg.permutation, groups, level)
    R = max(1, int(cfg.cv_repeats))
    cv_needed = bool(needs & {"probe", "frequency_topk"})
    if cv_needed:
        obs_folds, fold_strata = _fold_ids(np.repeat(a[None, :], R, axis=0), Y, cfg.n_folds, cv_rng, groups)
        null_folds, _ = _fold_ids(a_rows[1:], Y, cfg.n_folds, null_fold_rng, groups)
    else:
        fold_strata = "none"
    sizes = {}
    for yv in np.unique(Y):
        for g, nm in enumerate(names):
            sizes[f"Y={yv},A={nm}"] = int(((Y == yv) & (a == g)).sum())

    res = AuditResult(
        n=len(a),
        n_groups=G,
        groups=names,
        group_sizes=sizes,
        fold_strata=fold_strata,
        config=asdict(cfg),
        n_inconsistent_groups=n_mixed,
        attribute_level=level,
    )
    B = cfg.n_bootstrap
    for det in cfg.detectors:
        t0 = time.time()
        ci = (float("nan"), float("nan"))
        rep_sd, n_rep, note = float("nan"), 1, ""
        if det in {"probe", "frequency_topk"}:
            # observed: mean over R repeats of grouped CV; null: one repeat each (conservative)
            k_used = Kp if det == "probe" else K
            fn_cv = _stat_probe if det == "probe" else _stat_frequency
            # observed repeats are fitted in their own batch: the batched optimiser
            # stops on the mean objective, so sharing a batch with the null rows
            # would make the observed value depend on K
            reps, sc, tg = fn_cv(ctx, np.repeat(a[None, :], R, axis=0), obs_folds, cfg)
            null_stats, _, _ = fn_cv(ctx, a_rows[1 : k_used + 1], null_folds[:k_used], cfg)
            reps = np.asarray(reps, dtype=float)
            stats = np.r_[reps.mean(), null_stats]
            n_rep = R
            rep_sd = float(reps.std(ddof=1)) if R > 1 else float("nan")
            if B:
                per = sc.shape[1] // R
                b_r = int(math.ceil(B / R))
                boots = [
                    _bootstrap_auc(sc[:, r * per : (r + 1) * per], tg[:, r * per : (r + 1) * per], b_r, boot_rng, groups_idx)
                    for r in range(R)
                ]
                ci = bc_interval(np.concatenate(boots), float(stats[0]))
                note = "CI: resampling of out-of-fold predictions pooled over CV repeats, no refit; see repeat_sd"
        elif det == "statistical":
            stats = _stat_statistical(ctx, a_rows[: K + 1], cfg)
        else:
            fn = {
                "geometric": _stat_geometric,
                "bias_direction": _stat_bias_direction,
                "hbac_nmi": _stat_hbac_nmi,
            }[det]
            rows = a_rows[: K + 1]
            stats = fn(ctx, rows, cfg)
            if B:
                oh0 = _onehot(a[None, :], G)
                vals = []
                step = max(1, int(4e6 // max(len(a) * max(G, 2), 1)))
                for s in range(0, B, step):
                    m = min(step, B - s)
                    if groups_idx is None:
                        w = boot_rng.multinomial(len(a), np.full(len(a), 1.0 / len(a)), size=m)
                    else:
                        gw = boot_rng.multinomial(
                            len(groups_idx), np.full(len(groups_idx), 1.0 / len(groups_idx)), size=m
                        )
                        w = gw[:, ginv]
                    w = w.astype(np.float32)
                    vals.append(fn(ctx, rows[:1], cfg, w=w, oh_fixed=oh0))
                ci = bc_interval(np.concatenate(vals), float(stats[0]))
        obs, null = float(stats[0]), np.asarray(stats[1:], dtype=float)
        p = (1.0 + np.sum(null >= obs - 1e-12)) / (len(null) + 1.0)
        sdn = float(null.std(ddof=1)) if len(null) > 1 else float("nan")
        res.results[det] = DetectorResult(
            detector=det,
            statistic=obs,
            null_mean=float(null.mean()),
            null_sd=sdn,
            z=(obs - float(null.mean())) / sdn if sdn and sdn > 0 else float("nan"),
            p_value=float(p),
            ci_low=float(ci[0]),
            ci_high=float(ci[1]),
            n_permutations=int(len(null)),
            seconds=round(time.time() - t0, 3),
            note=note,
            repeat_sd=rep_sd,
            n_repeats=n_rep,
        )
    # the primary probe is judged at its own level; BH runs across the secondary detectors only
    if PRIMARY in res.results:
        pr = res.results[PRIMARY]
        pr.p_bh = float("nan")
        pr.flag = bool(pr.p_value < cfg.alpha)
    names_d = [d for d in res.results if d != PRIMARY]
    if names_d:
        q = benjamini_hochberg(np.array([res.results[d].p_value for d in names_d]))
        for d_, qv in zip(names_d, q, strict=True):
            res.results[d_].p_bh = float(qv)
            res.results[d_].flag = bool(qv < cfg.alpha)
    return res

conditional_permutations(
    a: ndarray,
    y: ndarray,
    k: int,
    rng: Generator,
    mode: str = "within_y",
    groups: ndarray | None = None,
    level: str = "patient",
) -> np.ndarray

Return a (k + 1, n) array whose row 0 is the observed attribute and rows 1..k are permuted copies: within each Y stratum, or globally when mode='global'.

With groups (patient ids) the permutation unit is the patient, because images of one patient are correlated and an image-level shuffle gives anti-conservative p-values.

level='patient': the attribute is a patient property. Each patient's value (its majority, which is also row 0) is reassigned among patients with the same Y pattern (all negative, all positive, or mixed).

level='image': the attribute varies between a patient's images (e.g. a marker). Whole attribute vectors (images ordered by Y) are reassigned among patients with the same sorted Y vector, hence the same image count, so the within-patient structure and the joint (A, Y) image counts are kept.

Source code in shortcut_detect/audit/conditional.py 
def conditional_permutations(
    a: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    k: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    mode: str = "within_y",
    groups: np.ndarray | None = None,
    level: str = "patient",
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return a (k + 1, n) array whose row 0 is the observed attribute and rows
    1..k are permuted copies: within each Y stratum, or globally when
    ``mode='global'``.

    With ``groups`` (patient ids) the permutation unit is the patient, because
    images of one patient are correlated and an image-level shuffle gives
    anti-conservative p-values.

    ``level='patient'``: the attribute is a patient property. Each patient's
    value (its majority, which is also row 0) is reassigned among patients with
    the same Y pattern (all negative, all positive, or mixed).

    ``level='image'``: the attribute varies between a patient's images (e.g. a
    marker). Whole attribute vectors (images ordered by Y) are reassigned among
    patients with the same sorted Y vector, hence the same image count, so the
    within-patient structure and the joint (A, Y) image counts are kept.
    """
    n = len(a)
    out = np.empty((k + 1, n), dtype=a.dtype)
    out[0] = a
    if groups is not None:
        _, ginv = np.unique(np.asarray(groups).astype(str), return_inverse=True)
        n_g = ginv.max() + 1
        if level == "image":
            buckets: dict[tuple, list[np.ndarray]] = {}
            for g in range(n_g):
                idx = np.flatnonzero(ginv == g)
                idx = idx[np.argsort(y[idx], kind="stable")]
                key = (len(idx),) if mode == "global" else tuple(int(v) for v in y[idx])
                buckets.setdefault(key, []).append(idx)
            mats = [np.stack(v) for v in buckets.values()]  # (patients, images)
            for i in range(1, k + 1):
                row = a.copy()
                for mat in mats:
                    row[mat] = a[mat[rng.permutation(len(mat))]]
                out[i] = row
            return out
        if level != "patient":
            raise ValueError("level must be 'patient' or 'image'")
        pa = np.empty(n_g, dtype=a.dtype)
        pstrat = np.empty(n_g, dtype=np.int64)
        y_hi = int(y.max())
        for g in range(n_g):
            idx = ginv == g
            vals, cnt = np.unique(a[idx], return_counts=True)
            pa[g] = vals[np.argmax(cnt)]
            ys = np.unique(y[idx])
            pstrat[g] = int(ys[0]) if len(ys) == 1 else y_hi + 1
        out[0] = pa[ginv]
        strata = [np.arange(n_g)] if mode == "global" else [np.flatnonzero(pstrat == s) for s in np.unique(pstrat)]
        for i in range(1, k + 1):
            prow = pa.copy()
            for idx in strata:
                prow[idx] = pa[idx][rng.permutation(len(idx))]
            out[i] = prow[ginv]
        return out
    strata = [np.arange(n)] if mode == "global" else [np.flatnonzero(y == v) for v in np.unique(y)]
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        row = a.copy()
        for idx in strata:
            row[idx] = a[idx][rng.permutation(len(idx))]
        out[i] = row
    return out

BH adjusted p-values along the last axis.

Source code in shortcut_detect/audit/conditional.py 
def benjamini_hochberg(p: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """BH adjusted p-values along the last axis."""
    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float)
    m = p.shape[-1]
    order = np.argsort(p, axis=-1)
    ranked = np.take_along_axis(p, order, axis=-1) * m / np.arange(1, m + 1)
    ranked = np.minimum.accumulate(ranked[..., ::-1], axis=-1)[..., ::-1]
    out = np.empty_like(ranked)
    np.put_along_axis(out, order, np.minimum(ranked, 1.0), axis=-1)
    return out

def swap_foregrounds(
    self,
    images: np.ndarray,
    foreground_masks: np.ndarray,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Produce augmented images by swapping foregrounds onto random backgrounds.

    Parameters
    ----------
    images : np.ndarray
        Images of shape (N, H, W) or (N, H, W, C), values in [0, 1].
    foreground_masks : np.ndarray
        Binary masks (N, H, W), 1 = foreground, 0 = background.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Augmented images, same shape as images.
    """
    images = np.asarray(images, dtype=np.float64)
    foreground_masks = np.asarray(foreground_masks, dtype=np.float64)
    need_squeeze = images.ndim == 3
    if need_squeeze:
        images = images[:, :, :, np.newaxis]
    if foreground_masks.ndim == 2:
        foreground_masks = foreground_masks[np.newaxis, ...]
    n, h, w, c = images.shape
    if (
        foreground_masks.shape[0] != n
        or foreground_masks.shape[1] != h
        or foreground_masks.shape[2] != w
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"foreground_masks shape {foreground_masks.shape} must match images (N={n}, H={h}, W={w})"
        )
    masks = (foreground_masks > 0.5).astype(np.float64)
    masks_exp = masks[:, :, :, np.newaxis] if masks.ndim == 3 else masks

    if n < 2:
        if need_squeeze:
            return images.squeeze(axis=-1)
        return images.copy()

    if self.augment_fraction < 1.0:
        n_aug = int(n * self.augment_fraction)
        if n_aug <= 0:
            if need_squeeze:
                return images.squeeze(axis=-1)
            return images.copy()
        indices = self._rng.choice(n, size=n_aug, replace=False)
    else:
        indices = np.arange(n)

    out = images.copy()
    for i in indices:
        j = self._rng.integers(0, n)
        while j == i and n > 1:
            j = self._rng.integers(0, n)
        background_j = images[j] * (1.0 - masks_exp[j])
        foreground_i = images[i] * masks_exp[i]
        out[i] = background_j + foreground_i

    if need_squeeze:
        out = out.squeeze(axis=-1)
    return np.clip(out, 0.0, 1.0).astype(np.float64)

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    effect_estimator: str = "direct",
    spurious_threshold: float = 0.1,
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> None:
    """
    Args:
        effect_estimator: Estimator for causal effect ("direct" supported).
        spurious_threshold: Attributes with |TE_a| < threshold are flagged
            as spurious. Default 0.1.
        random_state: Random seed for reproducibility.
    """
    super().__init__(method="causal_effect")
    if effect_estimator != "direct":
        raise ValueError(f"effect_estimator must be 'direct'; got '{effect_estimator}'.")
    if not 0.0 <= spurious_threshold <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError("spurious_threshold must be in [0, 1].")
    self.effect_estimator = effect_estimator
    self.spurious_threshold = spurious_threshold
    self.random_state = int(random_state)

    self.attribute_results_: list[AttributeEffectResult] = []

def fit(
    self,
    *,
    embeddings: np.ndarray,
    labels: np.ndarray,
    attributes: dict[str, np.ndarray],
    counterfactual_pairs: np.ndarray | list | None = None,
) -> CausalEffectDetector:
    """
    Fit causal effect estimator and detect spurious attributes.

    Args:
        embeddings: (n_samples, n_features) representation space.
        labels: (n_samples,) task labels (binary or multi-class).
        attributes: Dict of attribute_name -> (n_samples,) values per sample.
            Binary (0/1) or categorical; multi-valued attributes are binarized.
        counterfactual_pairs: Optional. For interventional data (Phase 2).
            Not used in current Direct estimator.

    Returns:
        self
    """
    X = np.asarray(embeddings, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(labels)
    if X.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError("embeddings must be 2D (n_samples, n_features)")
    if y.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError("labels must be 1D")
    if X.shape[0] != y.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("embeddings and labels must have same length")

    if not isinstance(attributes, dict) or not attributes:
        raise ValueError("attributes must be a non-empty dict of name -> (n,) array")

    n_samples = X.shape[0]
    for name, arr in attributes.items():
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
            raise ValueError("Attribute names must be non-empty strings")
        arr = np.asarray(arr)
        if arr.ndim != 1 or arr.shape[0] != n_samples:
            raise ValueError(f"attributes['{name}'] must be 1D of length {n_samples}")

    if counterfactual_pairs is not None:
        # Placeholder for Phase 2; Direct estimator ignores for now
        pass

    # Map labels to 0, 1, ... for binary/multi-class
    classes = np.unique(y)
    if len(classes) < 2:
        raise ValueError("At least 2 distinct labels are required")
    y_int = np.searchsorted(classes, y)

    attribute_results: list[AttributeEffectResult] = []

    for attr_name, attr_values in attributes.items():
        effect, n_a0, n_a1 = self._estimate_causal_effect_direct(X, y_int, attr_values)
        is_spurious = abs(effect) < self.spurious_threshold
        attribute_results.append(
            AttributeEffectResult(
                attribute_name=attr_name,
                causal_effect=effect,
                is_spurious=is_spurious,
                n_samples_a0=n_a0,
                n_samples_a1=n_a1,
            )
        )

    self.attribute_results_ = attribute_results

    n_spurious = sum(1 for r in attribute_results if r.is_spurious)
    if n_spurious > 1:
        shortcut_detected = True
        risk_level = "high"
        notes = f"Multiple attributes ({n_spurious}) have low causal effect (spurious)."
    elif n_spurious == 1:
        shortcut_detected = True
        risk_level = "moderate"
        spurious_names = [r.attribute_name for r in attribute_results if r.is_spurious]
        notes = f"Attribute '{spurious_names[0]}' has low causal effect (spurious)."
    else:
        shortcut_detected = False
        risk_level = "low"
        notes = "No attribute has estimated causal effect below threshold."

    effects_dict = {r.attribute_name: r.causal_effect for r in attribute_results}
    ranking = sorted(
        attribute_results,
        key=lambda r: abs(r.causal_effect),
        reverse=True,
    )

    metrics = {
        "n_attributes": len(attribute_results),
        "n_spurious": n_spurious,
        "spurious_threshold": self.spurious_threshold,
        "per_attribute_effects": effects_dict,
        "attribute_ranking": [r.attribute_name for r in ranking],
    }

    metadata = {
        "effect_estimator": self.effect_estimator,
        "random_state": self.random_state,
        "attribute_names": list(attributes.keys()),
    }

    report = {
        "per_attribute": [
            {
                "attribute_name": r.attribute_name,
                "causal_effect": r.causal_effect,
                "is_spurious": r.is_spurious,
                "n_samples_a0": r.n_samples_a0,
                "n_samples_a1": r.n_samples_a1,
            }
            for r in attribute_results
        ],
    }

    self._set_results(
        shortcut_detected=shortcut_detected,
        risk_level=risk_level,
        metrics=metrics,
        notes=notes,
        metadata=metadata,
        report=report,
    )
    self._is_fitted = True
    return self

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    config: CAVConfig | None = None,
    classifier: str = "logreg",
    random_state: int = 42,
    test_size: float = 0.2,
    min_examples_per_set: int = 20,

    cfg = config or CAVConfig(
        classifier=classifier,

        min_examples_per_set=int(min_examples_per_set),
        shortcut_threshold=float(shortcut_threshold),

    )

    if cfg.classifier != "logreg":

    if not 0.0 < cfg.test_size < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("test_size must be in (0, 1).")
    if cfg.min_examples_per_set < 2:
        raise ValueError("min_examples_per_set must be >= 2.")
    if not 0.0 <= cfg.shortcut_threshold <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError("shortcut_threshold must be in [0, 1].")
    if not 0.0 <= cfg.quality_threshold <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError("quality_threshold must be in [0, 1].")

    self.classifier = cfg.classifier
    self.random_state = int(cfg.random_state)
    self.test_size = float(cfg.test_size)
    self.min_examples_per_set = int(cfg.min_examples_per_set)
    self.shortcut_threshold = float(cfg.shortcut_threshold)

def fit(
    self,
    *,
    concept_sets: dict[str, np.ndarray],
    random_set: ArrayLike,
    target_activations: np.ndarray | None = None,
    target_directional_derivatives: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> CAVDetector:
    """Fit CAVs for concept-vs-random discrimination and compute TCAV metrics."""
    concept_sets_arr = self._validate_concept_sets(concept_sets)
    random_map = self._normalize_random_set(random_set, concept_sets_arr.keys())

    dim = next(iter(concept_sets_arr.values())).shape[1]
    target_acts_arr = self._validate_optional_matrix(
        target_activations, dim, "target_activations"
    )
    target_dd_arr = self._validate_optional_matrix(
        target_directional_derivatives,
        dim,
        "target_directional_derivatives",
    )

    concept_results: list[ConceptResult] = []
    cav_vectors: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    for concept_name, concept_examples in concept_sets_arr.items():
        random_examples = random_map[concept_name]
        self._validate_min_examples(concept_examples, random_examples, concept_name)

        X = np.vstack([concept_examples, random_examples])
        y = np.concatenate(
            [
                np.ones(concept_examples.shape[0], dtype=int),
                np.zeros(random_examples.shape[0], dtype=int),
            ]
        )
        X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
            X,
            y,
            test_size=self.test_size,
            stratify=y,
            random_state=self.random_state,
        )

        model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, random_state=self.random_state)
        model.fit(X_train, y_train)

        coef = np.asarray(model.coef_[0], dtype=float)
        norm = float(np.linalg.norm(coef))
        if norm <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError(f"Concept '{concept_name}' produced a zero-norm CAV vector.")
        cav_vector = coef / norm
        cav_vectors[concept_name] = cav_vector

        y_prob = model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]
        quality_auc = float(roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob))

        tcav_score: float | None = None
        if target_dd_arr is not None:
            directional = target_dd_arr @ cav_vector
            tcav_score = float(np.mean(directional > 0.0))

        activation_mean: float | None = None
        activation_p95: float | None = None
        if target_acts_arr is not None:
            projections = target_acts_arr @ cav_vector
            activation_mean = float(np.mean(projections))
            activation_p95 = float(np.percentile(projections, 95))

        flagged = (
            tcav_score is not None
            and quality_auc >= self.quality_threshold
            and tcav_score >= self.shortcut_threshold
        )

        concept_results.append(
            ConceptResult(
                concept_name=concept_name,
                n_concept=int(concept_examples.shape[0]),
                n_random=int(random_examples.shape[0]),
                quality_auc=quality_auc,
                tcav_score=tcav_score,
                activation_mean=activation_mean,
                activation_p95=activation_p95,
                flagged=bool(flagged),
            )
        )

    self.cav_vectors_ = cav_vectors
    self.concept_results_ = concept_results

    tcav_values = [r.tcav_score for r in concept_results if r.tcav_score is not None]
    quality_values = [r.quality_auc for r in concept_results]
    n_flagged = int(sum(1 for r in concept_results if r.flagged))

    if not tcav_values:
        shortcut_detected = None
        risk_level = "unknown"
        notes = "Directional derivatives were not provided; TCAV scores unavailable."
    else:
        max_tcav = float(max(tcav_values))
        if n_flagged > 0:
            shortcut_detected = True
            risk_level = "high" if max_tcav >= 0.75 else "moderate"
            notes = "At least one concept exceeded quality and TCAV thresholds."
        else:
            shortcut_detected = False
            risk_level = "low"
            notes = "No concept exceeded both quality and TCAV thresholds."

    metrics = {
        "n_concepts": int(len(concept_results)),
        "n_tested": int(len(tcav_values)),
        "max_tcav_score": float(max(tcav_values)) if tcav_values else None,
        "mean_tcav_score": float(np.mean(tcav_values)) if tcav_values else None,
        "max_concept_quality": float(max(quality_values)) if quality_values else None,
        "n_flagged": n_flagged,
        "shortcut_threshold": self.shortcut_threshold,
        "quality_threshold": self.quality_threshold,
    }

    metadata = {
        "classifier": self.classifier,
        "random_state": self.random_state,
        "test_size": self.test_size,
        "min_examples_per_set": self.min_examples_per_set,
        "concept_names": [r.concept_name for r in concept_results],
        "has_target_activations": target_acts_arr is not None,
        "has_target_directional_derivatives": target_dd_arr is not None,
    }

    report = {
        "per_concept": [self._concept_result_to_dict(result) for result in concept_results],
    }

    details = {
        "cav_vectors": {name: vec.tolist() for name, vec in cav_vectors.items()},
    }

    self._set_results(
        shortcut_detected=shortcut_detected,
        risk_level=risk_level,
        metrics=metrics,
        notes=notes,
        metadata=metadata,
        report=report,
        details=details,
    )
    self._is_fitted = True
    return self

Contrastive debiasing (Correct-n-Contrast) per Zhang et al. 2022.

Trains an encoder on embeddings via contrastive learning: anchors are from one (task, group) slice; positives are same task, different group; negatives are different task. This aligns representations to be invariant to spurious (group) signals while preserving task-relevant structure.

def fit(
    self,
    embeddings: np.ndarray,
    task_labels: np.ndarray,
    group_labels: np.ndarray,
) -> ContrastiveDebiasing:
    """
    Fit the contrastive debiasing model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    embeddings : np.ndarray
        Shape (n_samples, embed_dim).
    task_labels : np.ndarray
        Shape (n_samples,) – task/target labels.
    group_labels : np.ndarray
        Shape (n_samples,) – protected/group labels (spurious).

    Returns
    -------
    self : ContrastiveDebiasing
    """
    self._setup_seed()
    X = np.asarray(embeddings, dtype=np.float32)
    y = np.asarray(task_labels)
    g = np.asarray(group_labels)

    if X.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError("embeddings must be 2D (n_samples, embed_dim)")
    if y.ndim != 1 or g.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError("task_labels and group_labels must be 1D")
    if X.shape[0] != y.shape[0] or X.shape[0] != g.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("embeddings, task_labels, and group_labels must have same length")

    y_uniq = np.unique(y)
    g_uniq = np.unique(g)
    n_task = len(y_uniq)
    n_group = len(g_uniq)

    if n_group < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            "Contrastive Debiasing requires at least 2 groups. "
            "Positives are same-task, different-group samples."
        )
    if n_task < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            "Contrastive Debiasing requires at least 2 task classes for negatives."
        )

    y_map = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(y_uniq)}
    g_map = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(g_uniq)}
    y_idx = np.array([y_map[v] for v in y], dtype=np.int64)
    g_idx = np.array([g_map[v] for v in g], dtype=np.int64)

    batches = self._build_contrastive_batches(X, y_idx, g_idx, n_task, n_group)
    if not batches:
        raise ValueError(
            "Could not build contrastive batches. "
            "Ensure each task has samples in at least 2 groups."
        )

    embed_dim = X.shape[1]
    h_dim = self.hidden_dim
    if h_dim is None:
        h_dim = min(64, embed_dim)

    device = self._device()
    encoder = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(embed_dim, h_dim),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Dropout(self.dropout),
    ).to(device)
    task_head = nn.Linear(h_dim, n_task).to(device) if self.use_task_loss else None

    params = list(encoder.parameters())
    if task_head is not None:
        params.extend(list(task_head.parameters()))
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(params, lr=self.lr)
    ce = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

    X_t = torch.from_numpy(X).float().to(device)
    y_t = torch.from_numpy(y_idx).long().to(device)

    for _ in range(self.n_epochs):
        encoder.train()
        if task_head is not None:
            task_head.train()
        perm = np.random.permutation(len(batches))
        for idx in perm:
            a_ix, pos_ix, neg_ix, _ = batches[idx]
            n_pos = min(32, len(pos_ix))
            n_neg = min(32, len(neg_ix))
            p_perm = np.random.choice(len(pos_ix), size=n_pos, replace=n_pos > len(pos_ix))
            n_perm = np.random.choice(len(neg_ix), size=n_neg, replace=n_neg > len(neg_ix))
            pos_sel = pos_ix[p_perm]
            neg_sel = neg_ix[n_perm]

            anchor = X_t[a_ix : a_ix + 1]
            positives = X_t[pos_sel]
            negatives = X_t[neg_sel]

            all_vec = torch.cat([anchor, positives, negatives], dim=0)
            hidden = encoder(all_vec)
            z = F.normalize(hidden, dim=1)

            anchor_z = z[0:1]
            pos_z = z[1 : 1 + n_pos]
            neg_z = z[1 + n_pos :]

            sim_pos = torch.matmul(anchor_z, pos_z.T) / self.temperature
            sim_neg = torch.matmul(anchor_z, neg_z.T) / self.temperature
            # one InfoNCE term per positive, each against the negatives only
            logits = torch.cat([sim_pos.T, sim_neg.expand(n_pos, -1)], dim=1)
            labels_cl = torch.zeros(n_pos, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            loss_cl = F.cross_entropy(logits, labels_cl)

            loss = self.contrastive_weight * loss_cl
            if self.use_task_loss and task_head is not None:
                batch_ix = np.concatenate([[a_ix], pos_sel, neg_sel])
                y_batch = y_t[torch.from_numpy(batch_ix).to(device)]
                task_logits = task_head(hidden)
                loss_ce = ce(task_logits, y_batch)
                loss = loss + (1.0 - self.contrastive_weight) * loss_ce

            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss.backward()
            opt.step()

    self._encoder = encoder
    self._task_head = task_head
    self._embed_dim = embed_dim
    self._n_task = n_task
    self._task_map = y_map
    self._fitted = True
    return self
