Source code in shortcut_detect/ssa/ssa.py 
def fit(
    self,
    # DU: group-unlabeled
    du_embeddings: np.ndarray,
    du_labels: np.ndarray,
    # DL: group-labeled (has spurious attribute labels)
    dl_embeddings: np.ndarray,
    dl_labels: np.ndarray,
    dl_spurious: np.ndarray,
) -> SSADetector:
    """
    End-to-end SSA:
      Phase 1: pseudo-label spurious attribute for DU (Algorithm 1, Eq. 5–9).
      Phase 2: GroupDRO on pseudo-groups with validation on DL.
    """
    self._set_seed()
    cfg = self.config
    device = self._device()
    rng = np.random.RandomState(cfg.seed)

    # infer cardinalities
    n_y = int(max(np.max(du_labels), np.max(dl_labels))) + 1
    n_a = int(np.max(dl_spurious)) + 1
    G = n_y * n_a

    # Phase 1: Algorithm 1 pseudo-labeling with K folds
    du_ds = EmbeddingUnlabeledDataset(du_embeddings, du_labels)
    dl_full_ds = EmbeddingLabeledAttrDataset(dl_embeddings, dl_labels, dl_spurious)

    dl_train_idx, dl_val_idx = self._split_indices(len(dl_full_ds), cfg.dl_val_fraction, rng)
    dl_train_ds = torch.utils.data.Subset(dl_full_ds, dl_train_idx.tolist())
    dl_val_ds = torch.utils.data.Subset(dl_full_ds, dl_val_idx.tolist())

    dl_train_loader = build_loader(
        LoaderRequest(
            stage="dl_train",
            dataset=dl_train_ds,
            batch_size=cfg.batch_size,
            shuffle=True,
            num_workers=0,
            drop_last=False,
        ),
        loader_factory=cfg.loader_factory,
        stage_loader_overrides=cfg.stage_loader_overrides,
    )
    dl_val_loader = build_loader(
        LoaderRequest(
            stage="dl_val",
            dataset=dl_val_ds,
            batch_size=cfg.batch_size,
            shuffle=False,
            num_workers=0,
            drop_last=False,
        ),
        loader_factory=cfg.loader_factory,
        stage_loader_overrides=cfg.stage_loader_overrides,
    )

    folds = self._kfold_indices(len(du_ds), cfg.K, rng)
    a_hat_all = np.zeros(len(du_ds), dtype=np.int64)

    # Precompute DL^o group counts: |DL^o(g)| for g=(y,a)
    dl_y_train = dl_labels[dl_train_idx]
    dl_a_train = dl_spurious[dl_train_idx]
    dl_g_train = self._encode_group(dl_y_train, dl_a_train, n_a)
    dl_group_counts = np.bincount(dl_g_train, minlength=G).astype(np.int64)

    self.attr_models_.clear()

    for k in range(cfg.K):
        du_bullet_idx = folds[k]  # D_U^(k)
        du_circ_idx = np.concatenate([folds[j] for j in range(cfg.K) if j != k]).astype(
            np.int64
        )

        du_circ_ds = torch.utils.data.Subset(du_ds, du_circ_idx.tolist())
        du_bullet_ds = torch.utils.data.Subset(du_ds, du_bullet_idx.tolist())

        du_circ_loader = build_loader(
            LoaderRequest(
                stage="du_train",
                dataset=du_circ_ds,
                batch_size=cfg.batch_size,
                shuffle=True,
                num_workers=0,
                drop_last=False,
            ),
            loader_factory=cfg.loader_factory,
            stage_loader_overrides=cfg.stage_loader_overrides,
        )
        # a second loader (no shuffle) for threshold updates so subsampling is stable-ish
        du_circ_loader_eval = build_loader(
            LoaderRequest(
                stage="du_eval",
                dataset=du_circ_ds,
                batch_size=cfg.batch_size,
                shuffle=False,
                num_workers=0,
                drop_last=False,
            ),
            loader_factory=cfg.loader_factory,
            stage_loader_overrides=cfg.stage_loader_overrides,
        )
        du_bullet_loader = build_loader(
            LoaderRequest(
                stage="du_bullet",
                dataset=du_bullet_ds,
                batch_size=cfg.batch_size,
                shuffle=False,
                num_workers=0,
                drop_last=False,
            ),
            loader_factory=cfg.loader_factory,
            stage_loader_overrides=cfg.stage_loader_overrides,
        )

        d = du_embeddings.shape[1]
        model = AttrPredictor(d=d, n_a=n_a, hidden_dim=cfg.hidden_dim, dropout=cfg.dropout).to(
            device
        )

        opt = torch.optim.SGD(
            model.parameters(),
            lr=cfg.lr,
            momentum=cfg.momentum,
            weight_decay=cfg.weight_decay,
        )
        ce = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction="none")

        # initialize thresholds
        tau = np.full(G, cfg.tau_gmin, dtype=np.float32)

        # train loop for T iterations (Algorithm 1 lines 7–12) :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}
        it_dl = iter(dl_train_loader)
        it_du = iter(du_circ_loader)

        best_worst = -1.0
        best_state = None

        for t in range(1, cfg.T + 1):
            model.train()

            try:
                xL, yL, aL = next(it_dl)
            except StopIteration:
                it_dl = iter(dl_train_loader)
                xL, yL, aL = next(it_dl)

            try:
                xU, yU, _idxU = next(it_du)
            except StopIteration:
                it_du = iter(du_circ_loader)
                xU, yU, _idxU = next(it_du)

            xL = xL.to(device)
            aL = aL.to(device)
            xU = xU.to(device)

            # supervised loss on DL^o (Eq. 3/4 supervised term)
            logitsL = model(xL)
            loss_sup = ce(logitsL, aL).mean()

            # unsupervised loss on DU^o with group-wise threshold (Eq. 8)
            logitsU = model(xU)
            probsU = torch.softmax(logitsU, dim=1)
            confU, a_hatU = probsU.max(dim=1)

            # pseudo-group g_hat=(y, a_hat(x))
            yU_np = yU.numpy().astype(np.int64)
            a_hatU_np = a_hatU.detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.int64)
            g_hat_np = (yU_np * n_a + a_hatU_np).astype(np.int64)

            tau_batch = torch.from_numpy(tau[g_hat_np]).to(device)
            mask = (confU >= tau_batch).float()

            loss_unsup = (mask * ce(logitsU, a_hatU)).sum() / mask.sum().clamp_min(1.0)

            loss = loss_sup + loss_unsup

            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss.backward()
            opt.step()

            # update thresholds periodically (Algorithm 1 line 10; Eq. 7) :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
            if t % max(1, cfg.threshold_update_every) == 0:
                tau = self._compute_groupwise_thresholds(
                    model=model,
                    du_loader=du_circ_loader_eval,
                    dl_group_counts=dl_group_counts,
                    n_a=n_a,
                    tau_gmin=cfg.tau_gmin,
                    max_items=cfg.threshold_update_max_items,
                    device=device,
                )

            # optional: track best pseudo-labeler via worst-group attr acc on DL^bullet (Appendix A.3)
            if t % 200 == 0:
                worst = self._eval_attr_worst_group_acc(model, dl_val_loader, n_y, n_a, device)
                if worst > best_worst:
                    best_worst = worst
                    best_state = {
                        kk: vv.detach().cpu().clone() for kk, vv in model.state_dict().items()
                    }

        if best_state is not None:
            model.load_state_dict(best_state)

        self.attr_models_.append(model)

        # Predict pseudo-attributes on D_U^bullet (Algorithm 1 lines 13–14) :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
        model.eval()
        for xU, _yU, idxU in du_bullet_loader:
            xU = xU.to(device)
            logits = model(xU)
            pred_a = logits.argmax(dim=1).detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.int64)
            idxU_np = idxU.numpy().astype(np.int64)
            a_hat_all[idxU_np] = pred_a

    # Eq. (9): final pseudo-labels for all DU without threshold :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
    self.a_hat_ = a_hat_all

    # Phase 2: robust training on pseudo-groups, validate on DL (Section 4.3) :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}
    g_train = self._encode_group(du_labels, a_hat_all, n_a)
    g_val = self._encode_group(dl_labels, dl_spurious, n_a)

    group_ids = np.arange(G, dtype=np.int64)

    gdro = GroupDRODetector(cfg.groupdro)
    gdro.fit_with_val(
        train_embeddings=du_embeddings,
        train_labels=du_labels,
        train_group_labels=g_train,
        val_embeddings=dl_embeddings,
        val_labels=dl_labels,
        val_group_labels=g_val,
        group_ids=group_ids,
    )

    self.groupdro_ = gdro

    gdro_report = gdro.get_report()
    gdro_detail = gdro_report.get("report", {})
    final = gdro_detail.get("final", {})
    avg_acc = final.get("avg_acc", float("nan"))
    worst_acc = final.get("worst_group_acc", float("nan"))
    gap = (
        avg_acc - worst_acc if np.isfinite(avg_acc) and np.isfinite(worst_acc) else float("nan")
    )

    self.shortcut_detected_ = self.get_shortcut_detected(avg_acc, worst_acc)

    self.report_ = {
        "pseudo_attr_hat": a_hat_all,  # length |DU|
        "groupdro_report": gdro_detail,
    }
    metrics = {
        "n_labeled": int(len(dl_embeddings)),
        "n_unlabeled": int(len(du_embeddings)),
        "avg_acc": avg_acc,
        "worst_group_acc": worst_acc,
        "gap": gap,
    }
    metadata = {
        "K": cfg.K,
        "T": cfg.T,
        "tau_gmin": cfg.tau_gmin,
        "n_y": n_y,
        "n_a": n_a,
        "n_groups": G,
        "ssa_gap_threshold": cfg.ssa_gap_threshold,
    }
    if self.shortcut_detected_ is None:
        risk_level = "unknown"
    elif self.shortcut_detected_:
        risk_level = "moderate"
    else:
        risk_level = "low"

    self._set_results(
        shortcut_detected=self.shortcut_detected_,
        risk_level=risk_level,
        metrics=metrics,
        notes="SSA pseudo-labeling + GroupDRO gap-based detection.",
        metadata=metadata,
        report=self.report_,
    )
    self._is_fitted = True
    return self

def get_shortcut_detected(self, avg_acc: float, worst_acc: float) -> bool | None:
    """Detect a shortcut if worst-group gap exceeds threshold."""
    gap = avg_acc - worst_acc
    gap_thresh = self.config.ssa_gap_threshold
    if not np.isfinite(gap):
        return None
    return gap >= gap_thresh

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

comparison = next(iter(corrected["corrected_pvalues"]))
q = corrected["corrected_pvalues"][comparison]
significant = set(corrected["significant_features"][comparison] or [])

g0, g1 = np.unique(group_labels)[:2]

pooled = np.sqrt((x0.var(axis=0, ddof=1) + x1.var(axis=0, ddof=1)) / 2)
d = (x1.mean(axis=0) - x0.mean(axis=0)) / pooled

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
colors = ["red" if i in significant else "gray" for i in range(len(d))]
ax.scatter(d, -np.log10(q + 1e-300), c=colors, alpha=0.5)
ax.set_xlabel("Cohen's d")
ax.set_ylabel("-log10(BH-adjusted p)")

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    latent_dim: int = 10,
    kld_weight: float = 3.0,
    lr: float = 0.001,
    batch_size: int = 32,
    epochs: int = 50,
    classifier_epochs: int = 20,
    device: str | torch.device | None = None,
    predictiveness_threshold: float = 0.5,
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> None:
    """
    Args:
        latent_dim: VAE latent dimension.
        kld_weight: Beta-VAE KL weight (higher = more disentanglement).
        lr: VAE learning rate.
        batch_size: Training batch size.
        epochs: VAE training epochs.
        classifier_epochs: Classifier training epochs (frozen encoder).
        device: Device for training (cuda/cpu).
        predictiveness_threshold: Normalized predictiveness [0,1] above which
            a dimension is flagged as shortcut. Default 0.5 = top half.
        random_state: Random seed.
    """
    super().__init__(method="vae")
    self.latent_dim = int(latent_dim)
    self.kld_weight = float(kld_weight)
    self.lr = float(lr)
    self.batch_size = int(batch_size)
    self.epochs = int(epochs)
    self.classifier_epochs = int(classifier_epochs)
    self.device = torch.device(device or ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"))
    self.predictiveness_threshold = float(predictiveness_threshold)
    self.random_state = int(random_state)

    self._vae: ResnetVAE | None = None
    self._classifier: VAEClassifier | None = None
    self._latents_: np.ndarray | None = None
    self._labels_: np.ndarray | None = None

def fit(
    self,
    *,
    images: np.ndarray | torch.Tensor | None = None,
    labels: np.ndarray | torch.Tensor | None = None,
    img_size: int = 0,
    channels: int = 3,
    num_classes: int = 2,
    group_labels: np.ndarray | torch.Tensor | None = None,
    vae_checkpoint: str | None = None,
    train_dl: DataLoader | None = None,
    val_dl: DataLoader | None = None,
    test_dl: DataLoader | None = None,
) -> VAEDetector:
    """
    Fit VAE detector on images.

    Provide either (images, labels) or (train_dl, val_dl, test_dl).
    """
    if train_dl is not None and val_dl is not None:
        self._fit_from_dataloaders(
            train_dl=train_dl,
            val_dl=val_dl,
            test_dl=test_dl or val_dl,
            img_size=img_size,
            channels=channels,
            num_classes=num_classes,
            vae_checkpoint=vae_checkpoint,
        )
    else:
        if images is None or labels is None:
            raise ValueError("Provide images and labels, or train_dl/val_dl/test_dl.")
        self._fit_from_arrays(
            images=images,
            labels=labels,
            img_size=img_size,
            channels=channels,
            num_classes=num_classes,
            vae_checkpoint=vae_checkpoint,
        )

    latent_matrix = self._latents_
    labels_arr = self._labels_
    assert latent_matrix is not None
    assert labels_arr is not None

    mpwd = compute_mpwd_per_dimension(
        latent_matrix,
        labels_arr.astype(np.int64),
        self.latent_dim,
        num_classes,
    )

    predictiveness = compute_predictiveness_per_dimension(
        self._classifier,
        self.latent_dim,
    )

    # Normalize predictiveness to [0, 1] for thresholding
    pred_max = float(np.max(predictiveness))
    pred_norm = predictiveness / pred_max if pred_max > 0 else predictiveness

    _, flagged_indices = rank_candidate_dimensions(
        pred_norm,
        mpwd,
        self.predictiveness_threshold,
    )

    shortcut_detected = len(flagged_indices) > 0
    max_pred = float(np.max(pred_norm))
    n_flagged = len(flagged_indices)

    if shortcut_detected:
        risk_level = "high" if n_flagged >= self.latent_dim // 2 else "moderate"
        notes = f"{n_flagged} latent dimension(s) exceed predictiveness threshold."
    else:
        risk_level = "low"
        notes = "No latent dimension exceeded predictiveness threshold."

    per_dim = []
    for i in range(self.latent_dim):
        per_dim.append(
            {
                "dimension": i,
                "predictiveness": float(pred_norm[i]),
                "mpwd": float(mpwd[i]),
                "flagged": i in flagged_indices,
            }
        )

    metrics = {
        "n_candidate_dims": n_flagged,
        "max_predictiveness": max_pred,
        "n_flagged": n_flagged,
        "latent_dim": self.latent_dim,
    }

    metadata = {
        "kld_weight": self.kld_weight,
        "epochs": self.epochs,
        "predictiveness_threshold": self.predictiveness_threshold,
    }

    self._set_results(
        shortcut_detected=shortcut_detected,
        risk_level=risk_level,
        metrics=metrics,
        notes=notes,
        metadata=metadata,
        report={"per_dimension": per_dim},
        details={"mpwd": mpwd.tolist(), "predictiveness": pred_norm.tolist()},
    )
    self.shortcut_detected_ = shortcut_detected
    self._is_fitted = True
    return self

docs.title: Model comparison
docs.text:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from shortcut_detect import ShortcutDetector

models = {
    "ResNet50": np.load("embeddings_resnet50.npy"),
    "DenseNet121": np.load("embeddings_densenet121.npy"),
    "ViT-B/16": np.load("embeddings_vit.npy"),
}
task_labels = np.load("task_labels.npy")
group_labels = np.load("group_labels.npy")

rows = {}
for name, embeddings in models.items():
    detector = ShortcutDetector(methods=["probe", "statistical", "geometric"], seed=42)
    detector.fit(embeddings, task_labels, group_labels=group_labels)
    res = detector.get_results()
    rows[name] = {
        "probe_score": res["probe"]["results"]["metrics"]["metric_value"],
        "n_significant": sum(len(v or []) for v in res["statistical"]["significant_features"].values()),
        "effect_size": res["geometric"]["bias_pairs"][0].effect_size,
        "risk": res["probe"]["risk_value"],
    }

df = pd.DataFrame(rows).T
print(df)

For the paper's measurement per model, call conditional_audit(embeddings, group_labels, task_labels, config=cfg) in the same loop and compare result.results["probe"].statistic and its confidence interval. shortcut_detect.comparison.ModelComparisonRunner runs the detector loop above for the dashboard's comparison tab.

docs.title: Custom probe architectures
docs.text:
import torch.nn as nn
from shortcut_detect import TorchProbe

class AttentionProbe(nn.Module):
    """Probe with self-attention over the embedding."""

    def __init__(self, input_dim, n_classes, n_heads=4):
        super().__init__()
        self.attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(input_dim, n_heads, batch_first=True)
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(128, n_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = x.unsqueeze(1)                       # (batch, 1, dim)
        attn_out, _ = self.attention(x, x, x)
        return self.classifier(attn_out.squeeze(1))

probe = TorchProbe(
    model=AttentionProbe(512, 3),
    loss_fn=nn.CrossEntropyLoss(),
    device="cuda",      # None picks cuda when available, else cpu
    epochs=100,
)
probe.fit(embeddings, group_labels)
print(f"Held-out accuracy: {probe.metric_value_:.2%}")

docs.title: Linear debiasing
docs.text:
Project the direction between the two group centroids out of the embeddings, then measure again:

from shortcut_detect import GeometricShortcutAnalyzer, ShortcutDetector

analyzer = GeometricShortcutAnalyzer()
analyzer.fit(embeddings, group_labels)
pair = analyzer.bias_pairs_[0]
print(f"Original effect size: {pair.effect_size:.2f}")

g0, g1 = pair.groups
c0, c1 = analyzer.group_stats_[g0]["centroid"], analyzer.group_stats_[g1]["centroid"]
direction = (c1 - c0) / np.linalg.norm(c1 - c0)
embeddings_debiased = embeddings - np.outer(embeddings @ direction, direction)

analyzer_after = GeometricShortcutAnalyzer()
analyzer_after.fit(embeddings_debiased, group_labels)
print("After:", analyzer_after.summary_)   # the centroids now coincide, so bias_pairs_ is empty

def probe_and_count(X):
    detector = ShortcutDetector(methods=["probe", "statistical"], seed=42)
    detector.fit(X, group_labels)
    res = detector.get_results()
    return (res["probe"]["results"]["metrics"]["metric_value"],
            sum(len(v or []) for v in res["statistical"]["significant_features"].values()))

print("before (probe score, significant dims):", probe_and_count(embeddings))
print("after: ", probe_and_count(embeddings_debiased))

The package's own mitigations (AdversarialDebiasing, LastLayerRetraining, ContrastiveDebiasing in shortcut_detect.mitigation) have their own method pages.

docs.title: INLP (iterative null-space projection)
docs.text:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

def inlp_debias(embeddings, group_labels, n_iterations=10):
    X = embeddings.copy()
    for _ in range(n_iterations):
        clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X, group_labels)
        w = clf.coef_[0] / np.linalg.norm(clf.coef_[0])
        X = X - np.outer(X @ w, w)                     # project the direction out
        if LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X, group_labels).score(X, group_labels) < 0.55:
            break
    return X

embeddings_inlp = inlp_debias(embeddings, group_labels)

detector_inlp = ShortcutDetector(methods=["probe"], seed=42)
detector_inlp.fit(embeddings_inlp, group_labels)
print(f"After INLP: probe f1 {detector_inlp.get_results()['probe']['results']['metrics']['metric_value']:.2f}")

docs.title: Custom statistical tests
docs.text:
GroupDiffTest calls test(x1, x2) on each dimension and reads the p-value from the return value: a float, or a tuple whose second element is the p-value.

from scipy.stats import ks_2samp, f
from shortcut_detect import GroupDiffTest

test_ks = GroupDiffTest(test=ks_2samp)
test_ks.fit(embeddings, group_labels)
ks = test_ks.apply_correction(alpha=0.05, method="fdr_bh", verbose=False)
print("KS:", {k: len(v or []) for k, v in ks["significant_features"].items()})

def variance_ratio_test(group1, group2):
    """Two-sided F test on the variance ratio; returns (statistic, p-value)."""
    ratio = group1.var(ddof=1) / (group2.var(ddof=1) + 1e-10)
    df1, df2 = len(group1) - 1, len(group2) - 1
    p = 2 * min(f.cdf(ratio, df1, df2), 1 - f.cdf(ratio, df1, df2))
    return ratio, p

test_var = GroupDiffTest(test=variance_ratio_test)
test_var.fit(embeddings, group_labels)
var = test_var.apply_correction(alpha=0.05, method="fdr_bh", verbose=False)
print("variance ratio:", {k: len(v or []) for k, v in var["significant_features"].items()})

docs.title: Bootstrapped confidence intervals
docs.text:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.utils import resample
from shortcut_detect import SKLearnProbe

def bootstrap_probe_accuracy(X, y, n_bootstrap=100, seed=0):
    scores = []
    for i in range(n_bootstrap):
        X_boot, y_boot = resample(X, y, random_state=seed + i)
        probe = SKLearnProbe(LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000), metric="accuracy",
                             evaluation="holdout", test_size=0.2, random_state=seed + i)
        probe.fit(X_boot, y_boot)
        scores.append(probe.metric_value_)
    return np.mean(scores), np.percentile(scores, [2.5, 97.5])

mean_acc, (lo, hi) = bootstrap_probe_accuracy(embeddings, group_labels)
print(f"Probe accuracy {mean_acc:.2%} (95% interval {lo:.2%} to {hi:.2%})")

The audit computes a bias-corrected bootstrap interval for every detector statistic itself (ci_low and ci_high on each DetectorResult), so the paper's probe needs no extra loop.

docs.title: Batch processing
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
import json

def process_dataset(path):
    data = np.load(path)
    detector = ShortcutDetector(methods=["probe", "statistical"], seed=42)
    detector.fit(data["embeddings"], data["groups"])
    res = detector.get_results()
    return {
        "path": str(path),
        "n_samples": int(len(data["embeddings"])),
        "probe_score": float(res["probe"]["results"]["metrics"]["metric_value"]),
        "n_significant": sum(len(v or []) for v in res["statistical"]["significant_features"].values()),
        "risk": res["probe"]["risk_value"],
    }

results = [process_dataset(p) for p in sorted(Path("datasets/").glob("*.npz"))]
with open("batch_results.json", "w") as fh:
    json.dump(results, fh, indent=2)
print(pd.DataFrame(results).to_string())

docs.title: Basic usage examples
docs.text: This page walks through the package on synthetic data: the paper's audit first, then the ShortcutDetector pipeline and the four classic methods one at a time. Every snippet runs as written.

docs.title: Jupyter notebooks
docs.text:
The notebooks are in the repository:

cd examples/01_basic_usage/
jupyter lab

docs.title: Example 1: the audit
docs.text:
The paper's measurement. generate_linear_shortcut plants the group in the first few dimensions; the audit also needs a task label, so we draw one that is correlated with the group.

import numpy as np
from shortcut_detect import generate_linear_shortcut
from shortcut_detect.audit import AuditConfig, conditional_audit
from shortcut_detect.audit.report import audit_report, summary_text

X, group = generate_linear_shortcut(n_samples=1000, embedding_dim=128, shortcut_dims=5, seed=42)
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
task = np.where(rng.random(len(group)) < 0.3, 1 - group, group)   # task label correlated with the group

cfg = AuditConfig(n_permutations=200, n_permutations_probe=500, seed=42)
result = conditional_audit(X, group, task, config=cfg)

probe = result.results["probe"]
print(f"AUROC {probe.statistic:.3f}, null {probe.null_mean:.3f} (SD {probe.null_sd:.3f}), p = {probe.p_value:.3f}")
print(summary_text(result, attribute="group", task="task"))
audit_report(result, "audit.html", title="Synthetic audit", attribute="group", task="task")

docs.title: Example 2: the ShortcutDetector pipeline
docs.text:
from shortcut_detect import ShortcutDetector

detector = ShortcutDetector(methods=["hbac", "probe", "statistical", "geometric"], seed=42)
detector.fit(X, group)
print(detector.summary())

detector.generate_report("basic_report.html", format="html")

fit(embeddings, labels, group_labels=None) takes the task label as labels and the attribute as group_labels; with group_labels omitted the group-based methods use labels. To keep both: detector.fit(X, task, group_labels=group).

docs.title: Example 3: HBAC clustering
docs.text:
from shortcut_detect import HBACDetector

hbac = HBACDetector(max_iterations=3, min_cluster_size=0.05, random_state=42)
hbac.fit(X, group)

verdict = hbac.shortcut_report_["has_shortcut"]
print(f"Shortcut detected: {hbac.shortcut_detected_} ({verdict['confidence']} confidence, {verdict['types']})")
print(f"Linear test accuracy: {hbac.shortcut_report_['linearity_score']['test_accuracy']:.2f}")
for cluster in hbac.shortcut_report_["cluster_purities"]:
    print(f"  cluster {cluster['cluster_id']}: {cluster['size']} rows, purity {cluster['purity']:.2f}")

hbac.visualize(method="pca", save_path="hbac_pca.png")

docs.title: Example 4: probe-based detection
docs.text:
The probe splits the data itself (evaluation="holdout"), trains on one part and scores the other.

from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from shortcut_detect import SKLearnProbe

probe = SKLearnProbe(LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000), metric="accuracy",
                     evaluation="holdout", test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
probe.fit(X, group)

print(f"Held-out accuracy: {probe.metric_value_:.2%}")
print(f"Flagged: {probe.shortcut_detected_}, risk {probe.get_report()['risk_level']}")

docs.text:
from sklearn.svm import SVC
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

classifiers = {
    "Logistic Regression": LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000),
    "Linear SVM": SVC(kernel="linear"),
    "RBF SVM": SVC(kernel="rbf"),
    "Random Forest": RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42),
}

for name, clf in classifiers.items():

docs.title: Example 5: statistical testing
docs.text:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
from shortcut_detect import GroupDiffTest

test = GroupDiffTest(test=mannwhitneyu)
test.fit(X, group)
corrected = test.apply_correction(alpha=0.05, method="fdr_bh", verbose=False)

comparison = next(iter(corrected["significant_features"]))
significant = corrected["significant_features"][comparison] or []
q = corrected["corrected_pvalues"][comparison]
print(f"{comparison}: {len(significant)} of {X.shape[1]} dimensions significant after BH "
      f"({len(significant) / X.shape[1]:.1%})")
print("first significant dimensions:", significant[:10])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))
colors = ["red" if i in set(significant) else "gray" for i in range(len(q))]
ax.bar(range(len(q)), -np.log10(q + 1e-300), color=colors)
ax.axhline(-np.log10(0.05), color="blue", linestyle="--", label="q = 0.05")
ax.set_xlabel("dimension")
ax.set_ylabel("-log10(BH-adjusted p)")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("significant_dimensions.png", dpi=150)

docs.title: Example 6: geometric analysis
docs.text:
from shortcut_detect import GeometricShortcutAnalyzer

analyzer = GeometricShortcutAnalyzer(n_components=5)
analyzer.fit(X, group)
print(analyzer.summary_)

pair = analyzer.bias_pairs_[0]
print(f"effect size {pair.effect_size:.2f} between groups {pair.groups}")

# project onto the direction between the two centroids
g0, g1 = pair.groups
c0, c1 = analyzer.group_stats_[g0]["centroid"], analyzer.group_stats_[g1]["centroid"]
direction = (c1 - c0) / np.linalg.norm(c1 - c0)
projections = X @ direction

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))
for g in (g0, g1):
    ax.hist(projections[analyzer.group_stats_[g]["mask"]], bins=50, alpha=0.5, label=f"group {g}")
ax.set_xlabel("projection onto the bias direction")
ax.set_ylabel("count")
ax.set_title(f"effect size {pair.effect_size:.2f}")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("bias_projections.png", dpi=150)

docs.title: Example 7: with and without a shortcut
docs.text:
from shortcut_detect import ShortcutDetector, generate_linear_shortcut, generate_no_shortcut

X_biased, g_biased = generate_linear_shortcut(n_samples=500, embedding_dim=64, shortcut_dims=5, seed=42)
X_clean, g_clean = generate_no_shortcut(n_samples=500, embedding_dim=64, seed=42)

for name, (X_, g_) in {"biased": (X_biased, g_biased), "clean": (X_clean, g_clean)}.items():
    detector = ShortcutDetector(methods=["probe", "statistical"], seed=42)
    detector.fit(X_, g_)
    results = detector.get_results()
    score = results["probe"]["results"]["metrics"]["metric_value"]
    n_sig = sum(len(v or []) for v in results["statistical"]["significant_features"].values())
    print(f"{name}: probe f1 {score:.2f} ({results['probe']['risk_value']}), "
          f"{n_sig} significant dimensions ({results['statistical']['risk_value']})")

docs.title: Real data examples
docs.text:
This page shows the package on chest X-ray embeddings with demographic metadata.

Illustrative code

The file paths and printed values on this page illustrate the API; they are not results from the paper. The paper's CheXpert arrays (seven backbones over the first 2,000 images of the official train.csv, 477 patients) are on the gated Hugging Face dataset described in the paper's pipeline, and its measurement is shortcut_detect.audit.conditional_audit.

docs.title: Loading embeddings
docs.text:
The package ships no sample CSV. Two ways to get arrays:

From your own CSV in the dashboard's format (embedding_0 to embedding_{d-1}, task_label, group_label):

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

data = pd.read_csv("my_chexpert_embeddings.csv")
embedding_cols = [c for c in data.columns if c.startswith("embedding_")]
embeddings = data[embedding_cols].to_numpy()
task_labels = data["task_label"].to_numpy()    # e.g. pneumothorax 0/1
group_labels = data["group_label"].to_numpy()  # e.g. race

print(f"Samples: {len(data)}, embedding dim: {embeddings.shape[1]}, groups: {np.unique(group_labels)}")

From the paper's arrays, once you have access to the hub dataset (hf download MITCriticalData/ShortKit-ML-data --repo-type dataset --local-dir data/):

embeddings = np.load("data/chexpert_multibackbone/densenet121_embeddings.npy")
meta = pd.read_csv("data/chexpert_multibackbone/densenet121_metadata.csv")
task_labels = meta["task_label"].to_numpy()
group_labels = meta["sex"].to_numpy()          # the file also has "race" and "age_bin"

docs.title: The audit
docs.text:
from shortcut_detect.audit import AuditConfig, conditional_audit
from shortcut_detect.audit.report import audit_report, summary_text

cfg = AuditConfig(n_permutations=200, n_permutations_probe=500, seed=42)
result = conditional_audit(embeddings, group_labels, task_labels, config=cfg)   # add groups=patient_ids when patients repeat

print(summary_text(result, attribute="sex", task="the task label"))
audit_report(result, "chexpert_audit.html", title="DenseNet-121, sex", attribute="sex", task="the task label")

docs.title: Running the detector pipeline
docs.text:
from shortcut_detect import ShortcutDetector

detector = ShortcutDetector(methods=["hbac", "probe", "statistical", "geometric"], seed=42)
detector.fit(embeddings, task_labels, group_labels=group_labels)
print(detector.summary())

summary() prints one block per method with its risk label and reason, then the overall assessment (HIGH RISK, MODERATE RISK or LOW RISK under the default indicator_count condition). The numbers behind it are in get_results():

results = detector.get_results()
print(results["probe"]["risk_value"], results["probe"]["results"]["metrics"])
print(results["hbac"]["report"]["has_shortcut"])
print({k: len(v or []) for k, v in results["statistical"]["significant_features"].items()})
print(results["geometric"]["summary"])

dates = pd.to_datetime(data["date"])

docs.title: Interactive dashboard
docs.text: ShortKit-ML ships a Gradio web interface. Its first tab, Audit, runs the audit of the ShortKit-ML paper on your embeddings and writes the report. The other tabs (Detection, Model Comparison, Advanced Analysis) are the exploratory detector suite described further down.

docs.title: Launching the dashboard
docs.text:
# From a source checkout; Gradio is part of the base install
uv pip install -e .

# Launch the dashboard
python app.py

The dashboard opens at http://127.0.0.1:7860

docs.title: The Audit tab
docs.text:
The Audit tab asks the question of the ShortKit-ML paper: does the embedding carry the attribute beyond what the task label explains? It calls shortcut_detect.audit.conditional_audit with the settings you enter, so the result is the same one examples/walkthrough/03_run_the_audit.py prints, with a mouse instead of a script.

Captions are burned into the video; the audit's wait is cut from the recording.

What it takes

  • Embeddings: a .npy array of shape (n, d), or a CSV with embedding_0, embedding_1, ... columns (any numeric columns are used when none start with embedding_).
  • Labels CSV: one row per embedding, in the same order. Name the attribute column and the task column in the two boxes; a groups column is optional (a unit id per row, such as a patient or identity, kept whole in folds and permutations). Leave the labels file empty when the embeddings CSV already holds the label columns; the defaults, group_label and task_label, match the CSV convention of the Detection tab.
  • Settings: permutations K (200), probe permutations (500) and seed (42) are the paper's budget. Lower K for a quick look: 1500 CelebA embeddings at K = 100/200 take about half a minute on a laptop CPU, longer when the machine is busy. The two name boxes only change how the attribute and task are called in the summary and the report.
  • Load CelebA sample (1500 images) fills every input from data/celeba (ResNet-50 embeddings, attribute Male, task Blond_Hair; scripts/setup_celeba_data.py downloads them). Without those files it loads a synthetic set of 1500 embeddings with an attribute signal planted in the first four dimensions, and says so in the status line.

What it shows

  • A plain-language summary: the conditional probe's out-of-fold AUROC with its 95% interval, the permutation null's mean and SD, the permutation p-value and the decision at alpha = 0.05.
  • The detector table from AuditResult.rows(): statistic, interval, null mean and SD, p, Benjamini-Hochberg q and flag for the probe and the five secondary detectors (statistical, geometric, bias direction, HBAC NMI, frequency top-k). The probe decides; the other five describe and do not change the decision.
  • The six-panel figure: each detector's observed statistic (dot) against its null band (mean plus or minus 2 SD), red when flagged.
  • HTML report and PDF report downloads, both written by shortcut_detect.audit.report.audit_report, the same files examples/walkthrough/05_report.py produces.

The callback behind the Run button is a plain function, run_audit_tab(...) in app.py, so the same inputs can be run without Gradio (see tests/test_dashboard.py).

docs.title: Exploratory tabs
docs.text: The remaining tabs run the older ShortcutDetector suite with risk levels and an aggregation condition. They are exploratory: their thresholds and risk levels are heuristics for looking at an embedding space, and none of them decide anything in the ShortKit-ML paper, whose decision rule is the Audit tab's conditional probe.

docs.title: Sample data
docs.text:
The default data source of the Detection tab is Sample Data (CheXpert - Lightweight):

  • 2,000 rows drawn at random (random_state=42) from the CheXpert train.csv, with real metadata and demographics when Stanford's train.csv (and CHEXPERT DEMO.xlsx) are in data/; without them, 2,000 rows of synthetic metadata (sex, race, a Cardiomegaly label) are generated and the run is labelled "synthetic metadata"
  • 512-dimensional synthetic embeddings generated over that metadata (the first 10 dimensions carry a planted shortcut)
  • Race groups (WHITE, BLACK/AFRICAN AMERICAN, ASIAN, OTHER) from the demographics file
  • Tick Use real CheXpert embeddings to load data/chest_embeddings.npy, chest_labels.npy and chest_group_labels.npy instead, when they exist

These sample embeddings are not the arrays used in the paper; those are on the gated Hugging Face dataset described in Reproducing the Paper.

docs.title: Raw text mode
docs.text: With Input Mode set to Use Raw Data, upload a CSV with a text column and name a HuggingFace model (for example sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2); the dashboard embeds the text before running detection. This needs the hf extra (uv pip install -e ".[hf]"), which pins transformers>=4.39,<5.

docs.title: Custom data upload
docs.text:
Upload your own data as a CSV file:

embedding_0,embedding_1,embedding_2,...,task_label,group_label
0.123,0.456,0.789,...,1,group_a
0.234,0.567,0.890,...,0,group_b
...

Requirements:

  • Columns named embedding_0, embedding_1, etc. for embedding dimensions
  • Column named task_label for task labels (optional)
  • Column named group_label for protected attribute labels
  • Optional: attr_<name> columns (e.g., attr_race, attr_gender) for Causal Effect

docs.title: Detection methods
docs.text:
shortcut_detect/discovery.py registers 19 detection methods. The Detection tab's checklist shows sixteen of them (the first ten are selected by default); the other three, CAV, GradCAM mask overlap and VAE, run from the CAV concept-bundle accordion and the Advanced Analysis tab:

  • HBAC - Clustering analysis
  • Probe - Classifier-based detection
  • Statistical - Hypothesis testing
  • Geometric - Subspace analysis
  • Equalized Odds - TPR/FPR gaps across groups
  • GroupDRO - Worst-group robustness
  • Demographic Parity - Positive rate gaps across groups
  • Intersectional - Gaps across intersections of attributes (needs two or more attributes: attr_* columns, or group_label plus one attr_*)
  • Bias Direction PCA - Projection gap along the bias direction
  • Early-Epoch Clustering (SPARE) - Clusters of early-epoch representations
  • GCE - High-loss minority samples
  • SIS - Sufficient input subsets
  • SSA - Spread Spurious Attribute; the dashboard builds the labelled/unlabelled split (see SSA Settings)
  • Causal Effect - Spurious attribute detection (requires attr_* columns)
  • Frequency - Signal concentrated in few dimensions
  • Generative CVAE - Counterfactual embedding shifts

An Overall Assessment Condition dropdown picks how method results are aggregated (indicator_count by default), and a Multiple Testing Correction accordion sets the correction for the statistical test. These risk levels and conditions are the interactive detector's heuristics; the paper's audit (shortcut_detect.audit.conditional_audit, the Audit tab) uses the conditional probe with a permutation null instead, and none of the thresholds here decide anything in the paper.

Run Detection fits the selected methods and renders the results panel. Methods that fail or are skipped are listed in a method(s) did not run box with the error, rather than dropped silently. The HTML report includes a section per method, among them SSA and Generative CVAE sections when those methods ran.

docs.title: Visualizations
docs.text: The HTML report embeds PCA and t-SNE projections coloured by group, a 3D projection, dimension-importance and p-value heatmaps from the statistical test, and HBAC cluster purities.

docs.title: Model comparison
docs.text: The Model Comparison tab runs the same methods on two or more embedding sets (several CSVs, or several HuggingFace models over one raw-text CSV) and reports them side by side (Run Comparison).

docs.title: Advanced analysis
docs.text:
The Advanced Analysis tab holds optional tools that do not need a detection run first. Each accordion has one button:

Accordion Button What it does GradCAM Attention Overlap Generate GradCAM Heatmaps Heatmaps for uploaded images and a torch model GradCAM GT Mask Overlap Run Mask Overlap Overlap between heatmaps and ground-truth masks SpRAy Heatmap Clustering Run SpRAy Clustering Spectral clustering of heatmaps CAV Concept Testing Run CAV Analysis Concept activation vectors from a concept bundle VAE Image Shortcut Detection Run VAE Analysis VAE latent disentanglement on images Shortcut Feature Masking (M01) Run Shortcut Masking Mask or inpaint image regions, or zero/randomise embedding dimensions Background Randomization (M02) Run Background Randomization Swap foregrounds across backgrounds Adversarial Debiasing (M04) Run Adversarial Debiasing Gradient-reversal encoder; returns debiased embeddings as CSV Last Layer Retraining (M06 DFR) Run Last Layer Retraining Refits an L1 logistic head (C and penalty adjustable) on a subset balanced over attribute x task label groups (2A+Y), as in the paper; returns dfr_prediction Contrastive Debiasing (M07 CNC) Run Contrastive Debiasing Positives are same task, other group; negatives other task; returns debiased embeddings Explanation Regularization (M05 RRR) Run Explanation Regularization Penalises input gradients on shortcut regions; needs a model and images

The three embedding-level mitigations and DFR can read the embeddings exported by the last detection run (Use embeddings from last detection run) or an uploaded CSV with task_label and a group column. You can also include CAV in the main Detection report by uploading a concept bundle.

docs.title: Report export
docs.text:
Export your analysis:

  • HTML Report - Interactive report with all visualizations
  • PDF Report - Printable summary document
  • CSV Export - Raw results for further analysis (ZIP file)

docs.title: Method parameters
docs.text:
These are the controls exposed in the Detection tab's accordions; HBAC, Probe, Statistical and Geometric run with their package defaults and have no dashboard controls.

Parameter Default Description Significance level (alpha) 0.05 Alpha for the statistical test (0.01 to 0.10) Correction method fdr_bh Multiple testing correction: fdr_bh, bonferroni, holm, fdr_by SSA labeled fraction 0.2 Portion of samples treated as labeled for SSA (plus a split seed, 42) Frequency top percent / TPR / FPR 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.15 Dimension share kept and per-class flagging thresholds; probe evaluation on train Early-epoch clustering min cluster ratio 0.10 SPARE minimum cluster ratio GCE q / loss percentile / max iterations 0.7 / 90 / 500 Generalized cross-entropy settings Causal effect spurious threshold 0.1 Attributes with |effect| below this are flagged CAV concept quality threshold 0.7 Minimum concept AUC (Detection tab bundle and Advanced Analysis) VAE latent dimension 10 Advanced Analysis

Projections in the report (PCA, t-SNE, 3D) use fixed settings; there are no visualization controls in the dashboard.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: Run the paper's audit in a few minutes, then the other package methods.

docs.title: Step 1: prepare your data
docs.text:
The audit used in the paper needs four arrays:

  • Embeddings E: (n_samples, embedding_dim) - your frozen model's representations
  • Attribute A: (n_samples,) - the sensitive attribute (e.g., sex, race, age group)
  • Task label Y: (n_samples,) - the binary task label the audit conditions on
  • Patient ids groups: (n_samples,) - optional; needed whenever one patient has several images
import numpy as np

E = np.load("embeddings.npy")          # Shape: (1000, 512)
A = np.load("attribute.npy")           # Shape: (1000,), e.g. 0/1 or strings
Y = np.load("task_labels.npy")         # Shape: (1000,), 0/1
patient_ids = np.load("patients.npy")  # Shape: (1000,)

The width (512 here) is arbitrary: 2, 384, 4096 or any other size works. These four arrays are all the package needs, whatever model or modality (image, text, audio, tabular, multimodal) produced the embeddings.

docs.title: Step 2: run the conditional audit
docs.text:
from shortcut_detect.audit import AuditConfig, conditional_audit

cfg = AuditConfig(n_permutations=200, n_permutations_probe=500, seed=42)
result = conditional_audit(E, A, Y, config=cfg, groups=patient_ids)

probe = result.results["probe"]  # the primary test
print(f"Conditional probe AUROC: {probe.statistic:.3f} "
      f"(95% CI {probe.ci_low:.3f} to {probe.ci_high:.3f}), "
      f"permutation p = {probe.p_value:.3f}, flag = {probe.flag}")
print(f"Detectors flagged (descriptive): {result.n_flagged} of {len(result.results)}")

The probe predicts A from [E, Y]; its score is the out-of-fold AUROC and its p-value comes from shuffling A within strata of Y, between patients when groups is given. The five secondary detectors (statistical, geometric, bias_direction, hbac_nmi, frequency_topk) share that null and are reported as diagnostics. A flagged probe means the attribute is recoverable from the embedding given the task; whether a classifier uses it is a separate question. See the Audit API.

docs.title: Step 3: write the report
docs.text:
audit_report writes the audit as a self-contained HTML page or a PDF; the file extension picks the format. summary_text returns the one-paragraph verdict the report opens with.

from shortcut_detect.audit.report import audit_report, summary_text

print(summary_text(result, attribute="sex", task="pneumothorax"))

audit_report(result, "audit.html", title="ViT-B/16, sex given pneumothorax",
             attribute="sex", task="pneumothorax")
audit_report(result, "audit.pdf", title="ViT-B/16, sex given pneumothorax",
             attribute="sex", task="pneumothorax")

The report holds the summary paragraph, the setting (sample size, groups, permutations, alpha), one row per detector (statistic, 95% CI, null mean and SD, p, BH q, flag) and a figure of each statistic against its null. result.rows() returns the same table as a list of dicts, ready for a DataFrame or a CSV.

docs.title: Other package methods
docs.text: The ShortcutDetector pipeline predates the audit. It runs any of the package's 19 registered methods (shortcut_detect.discovery.available_method_plugins()), compares each against a fixed threshold and aggregates the flags into a LOW, MODERATE or HIGH label. It drives the dashboard, the MCP server's detection tools and the HTML, PDF and Markdown reports. It does not condition on the task label, and none of its thresholds decides anything in the paper: use it to explore, and the audit to measure.

docs.title: Several methods at once
docs.text:
from shortcut_detect import ShortcutDetector, generate_linear_shortcut

# 500 embeddings of width 64; the first 5 dimensions separate the two groups
X, group = generate_linear_shortcut(n_samples=500, embedding_dim=64, shortcut_dims=5, seed=42)

detector = ShortcutDetector(methods=["hbac", "probe", "statistical", "geometric"], seed=42)
detector.fit(X, group)
print(detector.summary())

results = detector.get_results()
print(results["probe"]["risk_value"], results["probe"]["results"]["metrics"]["metric_value"])

detector.generate_report("shortcut_report.html", format="html")   # also "pdf" and "markdown"

fit(embeddings, labels, group_labels=None) takes the task label as labels and the attribute as group_labels. When group_labels is omitted, the group-based methods use labels, which is what the call above does. generate_no_shortcut(n_samples=500, embedding_dim=64, seed=42) is the matching negative control.

docs.title: One method at a time
docs.text:
Each method is also a class with fit, shortcut_detected_, get_report() and summary().

HBAC splits the embeddings with k-means a few times, then checks cluster purity and linear separability:

from shortcut_detect import HBACDetector

hbac = HBACDetector(max_iterations=3, min_cluster_size=0.05, random_state=42)
hbac.fit(X, group)

verdict = hbac.shortcut_report_["has_shortcut"]
print(hbac.shortcut_detected_, verdict["confidence"], verdict["types"])
print(f"linear test accuracy {hbac.shortcut_report_['linearity_score']['test_accuracy']:.2f}")
print([round(c["purity"], 2) for c in hbac.shortcut_report_["cluster_purities"]])

The probe trains a classifier to predict the group from the embedding and scores it on a held-out split:

from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from shortcut_detect import SKLearnProbe

probe = SKLearnProbe(LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000), metric="accuracy",
                     evaluation="holdout", test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
probe.fit(X, group)
print(f"held-out accuracy {probe.metric_value_:.3f}, flagged: {probe.shortcut_detected_}")

The statistical test compares the groups dimension by dimension and corrects for multiple testing:

from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
from shortcut_detect import GroupDiffTest

test = GroupDiffTest(test=mannwhitneyu)
test.fit(X, group)
corrected = test.apply_correction(alpha=0.05, method="fdr_bh", verbose=False)
comparison, significant = next(iter(corrected["significant_features"].items()))
print(f"{comparison}: {len(significant or [])} of {X.shape[1]} dimensions differ after BH correction")

The geometric analyzer measures how far the group centroids sit apart and how much the groups' principal subspaces overlap:

from shortcut_detect import GeometricShortcutAnalyzer

geo = GeometricShortcutAnalyzer(n_components=5)
geo.fit(X, group)
pair = geo.bias_pairs_[0]
print(geo.summary_["risk_level"], f"effect size {pair.effect_size:.2f} for groups {pair.groups}")
print(f"mean subspace cosine {geo.subspace_pairs_[0].mean_cosine:.2f}")

docs.title: Fixed thresholds
docs.text:
These are the rules each class applies; they are heuristics for exploration.

Method Flagged when Default settings HBAC two or more clusters have purity above 0.8, or few dimensions matter and the linear test accuracy is above 0.85 max_iterations=3, min_cluster_size=0.01 Probe the held-out metric exceeds threshold metric="f1", threshold=0.70 Statistical any dimension stays significant after correction apply_correction(alpha=0.05, method="fdr_bh") Geometric a centroid pair has effect size at or above effect_threshold, or a subspace pair has mean cosine at or above subspace_cosine_threshold 0.8 and 0.85

docs.title: Embedding-only mode
docs.text:
For systems that only expose embeddings (for example a Hugging Face inference endpoint), pass the raw inputs and an embedding source:

from shortcut_detect import ShortcutDetector, HuggingFaceEmbeddingSource

texts = ["patient has mild edema", "normal study", ...]
labels = np.array([1, 0, ...])
groups = np.array([0, 1, ...])

hf_source = HuggingFaceEmbeddingSource(
    model_name="sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
    pooling="mean",
    batch_size=32,
)

detector = ShortcutDetector(methods=["probe", "statistical"])
detector.fit(
    embeddings=None,  # triggers embedding-only mode
    labels=labels,
    group_labels=groups,
    raw_inputs=texts,
    embedding_source=hf_source,
    embedding_cache_path="embeddings.npy",  # optional cache
)

This needs the hf extra. See the embedding sources API for CallableEmbeddingSource and caching.

docs.title: Walkthrough: audit an embedding, step by step
docs.text:
This page is the whole workflow of the ShortKit-ML paper's audit on one public data set, CelebA ResNet-50 embeddings, from a fresh install to the PDF report. Every recording below is a real terminal session (tap one to open it full size on a phone); the scripts it runs are in examples/walkthrough/, so you can replay each step on your own data by changing one path.

The question the audit answers: does an embedding carry a sensitive attribute beyond what the task label explains? If it does, a classifier trained on that embedding could take a shortcut through the attribute. The audit measures this shortcut potential with one calibrated test; whether a particular classifier uses it is a separate experiment.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
pip install shortkit-ml gives you the package; the clone below adds the examples and the sample data. About ten seconds with uv when the wheels are cached; pip install -e . works the same way.

git clone https://github.com/criticaldata/ShortKit-ML.git && cd ShortKit-ML
uv venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .

docs.title: 2. What the audit needs
docs.text:
Four arrays, three of them required:

Array Shape Meaning E (n, d) float one embedding per row, from any encoder, any width d A (n,) the sensitive attribute (sex, age group, race, site, scanner) Y (n,) the task label the classifier would learn groups (n,), optional a unit id (patient, identity) when one unit has several rows

A and Y are usually correlated in clinical data, so a plain probe for A would partly read Y. The audit conditions on Y and asks the sharper question.

E = np.load("data/celeba/celeba_real_embeddings.npy")       # (10000, 2048)
att = pd.read_csv("data/celeba/celeba_real_attributes.csv")  # same row order
A = att["Male"].to_numpy()
Y = att["Blond_Hair"].to_numpy()

docs.title: 3. Any file, any encoder, any modality
docs.text:
The audit sees only the matrix. Embeddings saved as .npy, .csv, .parquet or a torch tensor all load to the same (n, d) array, and the width is whatever your encoder produced: 384 from a sentence model, 8 from a tabular model, 2048 from ResNet-50.

The only rules: E is 2-D float with finite values; A, Y and groups have one entry per row of E, in the same order.

docs.title: 4. Run the audit
docs.text:
conditional_audit fits the primary test, a logistic probe predicting A from [E, Y], scores it by out-of-fold AUROC, and calibrates it by permuting A within levels of Y (between patients when groups is given). Five secondary detectors share that null and are reported as diagnostics. Default budget as in the paper: 500 permutations for the probe, 200 for the rest; about 40 s for 2,000 images of width 2,048 on a laptop CPU.

from shortcut_detect.audit import AuditConfig, conditional_audit

cfg = AuditConfig(n_permutations=200, n_permutations_probe=500, seed=42)
result = conditional_audit(E, A, Y, config=cfg)          # groups=patient_ids when needed
probe = result.results["probe"]
print(probe.statistic, probe.ci_low, probe.ci_high, probe.p_value, probe.flag)

How to read it: the probe AUROC is the score; the null mean is what that score looks like when A carries no information beyond Y; the permutation p says whether the observed score is unusual under that null. The probe decides at p < 0.05. The secondary detectors are flagged at Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.05 across the five and describe the signal; they never change the decision.

docs.title: 5. Why conditioning matters
docs.text:
On data where A follows Y ninety per cent of the time but the embedding encodes only Y, an unconditional probe fires (it reads A through Y), while the conditional audit stays at its null. Plant an A signal and the conditional audit fires.

Under a true null the conditional probe rejected 2 to 3 per cent of synthetic data sets in the paper; the unconditional probe rejected 95 per cent at the same correlation.

docs.title: 6. The report
docs.text:
audit_report writes the same audit as a self-contained HTML page or a two-page PDF: the setting, a plain-language verdict, the detector table against the null, and one panel per detector.

from shortcut_detect.audit.report import audit_report

audit_report(result, "celeba_audit.html", attribute="Male", task="Blond_Hair")
audit_report(result, "celeba_audit.pdf", attribute="Male", task="Blond_Hair")

docs.title: 7. The same audit in the dashboard
docs.text:
The tour in one video: install, bring your embeddings (any encoder, any modality), then the dashboard's Audit tab from a clean terminal (python app.py, the CelebA sample, the run, the verdict and the table, the PDF downloaded and read to the end), and the MCP call for agents.

python app.py        # opens http://127.0.0.1:7860, Audit tab first

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text:
Shortcut detection and mitigation methods, each scored by the same code on the same benchmark with planted shortcuts of known strength. Four tracks, scored separately: an embedding method and an image method are never ranked against each other.

Have a method? Add it in one folder and one pull request: how to submit. CI scores it on the benchmark and your entry appears here, with your name and paper, when it is merged.

Separate from the paper's audit

The leaderboard measures methods on synthetic benchmarks. It does not change what conditional_audit, the package's calibrated test, reports. The benchmark's rules and metrics are on the tracks page.

docs.title: Embedding detection
docs.text:
Given embeddings E, an attribute A and a task label Y, score whether E carries A beyond what Y explains. Null datasets have A correlated with Y but no extra attribute signal, so a method that only finds the correlation scores 0.5. Ranked by AUROC, after grouping: entries whose flag fires on at most 20% of null datasets first, then entries without a flag, then entries whose flag fires more often. Benchmark v1.1. Track rules.

Train a task classifier on embeddings where the attribute predicts the label in training (rho >= 0.9) but not at test time (rho = 0.5). Scored by worst-group accuracy on the test set. Ranked by Worst-group acc. Benchmark v1.0. Track rules.

docs.text:
